title: fix(scripts): Strip trailing line comments before `@import` parsing
description:
## Summary

The new bs5 update in bslib makes `make upgrade-html-deps` fail because of a comment shipped in the copied scss from bs5.

Example of the error in practice:
```
  ── Prepare 28 Bootstrap theme presets ──

  ℹ Prepare bootstrap theme Sass files...
  Error in theme_files_used(lines) :
    Could not find file: variables-dark // TODO:
  can be removed safely in v6, only here to avoid
   breaking changes in v5.3
  Calls: prepare_and_write_theme_sass_files ...
  theme_files_used -> <Anonymous> -> force ->
  theme_files_used
  ✖ Failed to prepare bootstrap theme Sass files.
   [54ms]

  Execution halted
  Ran 2/2 deferred expressions
  make: *** [upgrade-html-deps] Error 1
```

This currently triggers on upstream bslib's `inst/lib/bs5/scss/_variables.scss`, which contains:

```scss
@import "variables-dark"; // TODO: can be removed safely in v6, only here to avoid breaking changes in v5.3
```

`theme_files_used()` then tries to resolve a file literally named `variables-dark // TODO: can be removed safely in v6, …` and aborts.

## Fix

Strip `\s*//.*$` from each candidate import line *before* the path-extraction `gsub`s, so trailing line comments no longer leak into the matched filename. One-line change.

## Risk analysis

**Low risk overall.** A few edge cases to note:

- **`//` in import URLs** — The regex `\s*//.*$` strips from the first `//` with optional leading whitespace. If any imported file were a URL like `@import "http://example.com/reset.css";`, this would mangle the path. In practice this doesn't apply — `theme_files_used` resolves local filesystem paths for Bootstrap/bslib SCSS files, so URL imports don't arise.
- **Block comments not handled** — `/* block comment */` after an import would not be stripped. This isn't a concern with current bslib, but worth noting for future resilience.
- **`sub` vs `gsub`** — Using `sub` (replace first match) is appropriate here since the pattern `\s*//.*$` anchors to end-of-line and each line has at most one trailing comment.

## Notes

Running `make upgrade-html-deps` against the current `rstudio/bslib@main` also picks up a new Bootswatch theme, **`brite`**, as well as additional changes from the minor Bootstrap upgrade. These changes have been moved to a separate PR for review.

## Test plan

- [x] Verify `make upgrade-html-deps` completes successfully on current `rstudio/bslib@main`
- [x] Moved the vendored changes to a separate PR, since there's a bit more in there I want to check. ~~Verify the generated `shiny/www/shared/sass/` tree looks unchanged vs. the previous successful run (no missing/extra imports)~~

title: fix: Make data grid styles adapt to dark mode (#1635)
description:
## Summary

Fixes #1635. When `ui.input_dark_mode()` was combined with `@render.data_frame` / `render.DataGrid()`, the column header and hover-row backgrounds stayed near-white in dark mode while the text flipped to a light gray — producing unreadably low contrast.

The fix is a four-line edit in `js/data-frame/styles.scss` that swaps fixed light/dark color tokens for Bootstrap 5.3 mode-aware tokens (with legacy fallbacks so older bslib themes still work):

| Variable | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--shiny-datagrid-grid-header-bgcolor` | `var(--bs-light, #eee)` | `var(--bs-tertiary-bg, #eee)` |
| `--shiny-datagrid-grid-body-selected-bgcolor` | `#b4d5fe` | `var(--bs-primary-bg-subtle, #b4d5fe)` |
| `--shiny-datagrid-grid-body-selected-color` | `var(--bs-dark)` | `var(--bs-emphasis-color, var(--bs-dark))` |
| `--shiny-datagrid-table-cell-edit-saving-color` | `var(--bs-gray-500)` | `var(--bs-secondary-color, var(--bs-gray-500))` |

The header bg change cascades to the row-hover bg, the row-number column, and the color-mixed header-selected bg.

Also adds:
- Playwright regression tests under `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/dark_mode/` that assert luminance and WCAG contrast on the column header and hovered row in dark mode.
- A CHANGELOG entry.

A standalone screenshot harness used to generate the before/after PNGs lives in the PR comment below (not checked in).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/dark_mode/` — both regression tests pass (luminance < 0.5 and WCAG contrast ≥ 4.5 in dark mode).
- [x] `make js-build` produces a bundle containing the four new Bootstrap tokens.
- [x] Manual visual verification via the screenshot harness (light/dark × default/hover/selected/editing) — see comment below.
- [x] Sanity-check the rest of the data-frame Playwright suite is unaffected by the SCSS change.

ci: Cache Playwright Docker image between runs
description:
This pull request introduces an image caching mechanism to the Playwright setup workflow in `.github/py-shiny/setup-playwright-remote/action.yaml` to speed up CI runs by avoiding redundant image pulls. Additionally, it refactors a Playwright test utility in `test_stream_basic.py` for improved reliability and readability.

**CI/CD improvements:**

* Added steps to compute a cache key, restore, load, save, and persist the Playwright Docker image using GitHub Actions cache, reducing redundant downloads and potentially speeding up CI runs. (.github/py-shiny/setup-playwright-remote/action.yaml)

**Testing improvements:**

* Refactored the scroll-to-bottom check in `test_stream_basic.py` by replacing the `is_element_scrolled_to_bottom` function with `expect_element_scrolled_to_bottom`, which uses Playwright's `wait_for_function` for more robust and reliable assertions. 
* Cache key includes the resolved Playwright version + runner.os/runner.arch, so each Playwright bump invalidates cleanly.
- On cache hit, the image tar is loaded with docker load and the MCR pull is skipped entirely.
- On cache miss, the existing retry-with-backoff pull runs, then the image is saved with docker save and uploaded with actions/cache/save.
- Restore/save are split so a successful restore doesn't re-upload, and the save only runs when an actual pull happened.

title: fix: Always invalidate server-side input values for incoming wire messages

The `test-narwhals-integration` CI job was still installing Playwright browsers locally (`playwright install --with-deps chromium`), which is slow.
```yaml
- name: Narwhals integration setup

  uses: posit-dev/py-shiny/.github/py-shiny/narwhals-test@main
```

Both actions require `uv` to be installed (verified at runtime) and `shiny-dir` is a required input.

title: feat: Add session.destroy() to clean up dangling reactivity
description:
Closes #2207

## Summary

When dynamic UI is removed (e.g., via `ui.remove_ui()`), the server-side reactive objects created for that UI — effects, calcs, values, inputs, and outputs — continue to persist and execute. This "dangling reactivity" wastes resources and can cause errors.

This PR adds `session.destroy()` and `session.on_destroy()`, which destroy all reactive state associated with a module scope and all descendant module scopes. Reactive objects self-register weak cleanup callbacks during `__init__`, so destruction is automatic and comprehensive, while still allowing garbage collection of unreferenced reactive objects before session end.

## What `session.destroy()` cleans up

Calling `await session.destroy()` on a `SessionProxy` removes all namespaced state from the root session:

- **Effects** — Stopped permanently (will never re-execute).
- **Calcs** — Invalidated and destroyed. Subsequent calls raise `DestroyedReactiveError`.
- **Values** — Invalidated and destroyed. After destruction:
  - `get()` / `set()` / `unset()` / `freeze()` raise `DestroyedReactiveError`
  - `is_set()` returns `False` (allows defensive checks without raising)
  - `destroy()` is idempotent (no-op on second call)
- **Inputs** — Namespaced input keys and their values are removed from the shared input map. A new module with the same namespace gets fresh input values.
- **Outputs** — Namespaced output entries are removed and their render effects destroyed.
- **Message handlers** — Namespaced entries removed from root session.
- **Dynamic routes** — Namespaced entries removed from root session.
- **Downloads** — Namespaced entries removed from root session.
- **Descendant scopes** — All child/grandchild namespaces are also destroyed, depth-first (children before parents).

Destroy does **not** alter the UI — use `ui.remove_ui()` for that. Destroy only cleans up the reactive graph and server-side registrations.

## Example

```python
@module.server
def panel_server(input, output, session, panel_num, on_remove):
    counter = reactive.value(0)

    # Register cleanup callback — runs when session.destroy() is called
    session.on_destroy(on_remove)

    @reactive.effect
    def auto_increment():
        reactive.invalidate_later(1)
        with reactive.isolate():
            counter.set(counter.get() + 1)

    @reactive.calc
    def derived():
        return f"Count is {counter.get()}"

    @render.text
    def status():
        return derived()

    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.remove)
    async def handle_remove():
        ui.remove_ui(selector=f"div#{session.ns('container')}")
        await session.destroy()  # Clean up ALL reactive state for this module
```

A full demo app is included at `tests/playwright/shiny/bugs/2207-dangling-reactivity/app.py`.

## Public API added

### `Session` (ABC)

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `on_destroy(fn)` | Register a callback to run when this session or module scope is destroyed. For `SessionProxy`, callbacks fire on explicit `destroy()`. For `AppSession`, callbacks fire at session end after `on_ended`. |
| `destroy()` | Destroy this session or module scope. Idempotent. Does not alter UI. |

### `reactive.Value.destroy()`

Invalidates and destroys the value. After destruction, `get()`/`set()`/`unset()`/`freeze()` raise `DestroyedReactiveError`; `is_set()` returns `False`. Idempotent. Works on read-only values (e.g., input values). Auto-registered with session via weak callback.

### `reactive.Calc_.destroy()`

Invalidates context and all downstream dependents. After destruction, calling the calc raises `DestroyedReactiveError`. Idempotent. Auto-registered with session via weak callback.

### `DestroyedReactiveError`

Exception raised when accessing a destroyed `Value` or `Calc_`.

## Architecture

- **Self-registration with weak callbacks**: Each `Value`, `Calc_`, and `Effect_` registers its `destroy()` method via `session.on_destroy()` during `__init__`, wrapped in `weakref.WeakMethod`. This allows garbage collection of unreferenced reactive objects before session end — the session holds only a weak reference, not a strong one.
- **Root session storage**: Destroy callbacks live on `AppSession._destroy_callbacks_by_ns`, keyed by namespace string. A shared `_invoke_destroy_callbacks()` helper handles namespace traversal for both `AppSession.destroy()` and `SessionProxy.destroy()`.
- **Descendant cascade**: `destroy()` uses prefix matching to find all child/grandchild namespaces, fires callbacks depth-first (most nested first), then cleans up inputs, outputs, message handlers, dynamic routes, and downloads.
- **Namespace reuse**: After `destroy()`, the namespace is freed. A new module with the same namespace gets fresh state.
- **`AppSession.on_destroy()` / `destroy()`**: `AppSession` stores and invokes destroy callbacks (using namespace key `""`). At session end, `destroy()` is called after `on_ended` callbacks so that `on_ended` handlers can still read reactive state.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `tests/pytest/test_destroy.py` covering:
  - Value/Calc/Effect destroy behavior (DestroyedReactiveError, idempotency, invalidation)
  - Inputs/Outputs cleanup (namespace removal, resurrection, preservation of other namespaces)
  - SessionProxy destroy (callbacks, message handlers, dynamic routes, downloads cleanup)
  - Descendant cascade ordering (depth-first, no sibling/parent cascade)
  - Self-registration via weak callbacks (Value, Calc, Effect)
  - Garbage collection (Value/Calc/Effect GC'd when unreachable despite session registration; dead callbacks silently skipped)
  - Module re-creation (same namespace gets fresh state)
  - AppSession and ExpressStubSession behavior
- [x] 6 Playwright e2e tests in `tests/playwright/shiny/bugs/2207-dangling-reactivity/`
- [x] Manual testing with demo app

title: ci: Add remote Playwright action and CI usage
description:
Linux Playwright CI jobs now connect to a prebuilt browser environment running in Docker instead of installing browsers locally on the runner each time. 
This reduces CI startup time by eliminating the playwright install `--with-deps` step and is more reliable since it uses Microsoft's official pre-built Playwright image. 

Local development is unchanged.

### What changed and why

`.github/py-shiny/setup-playwright-remote/action.yaml`
A repo-owned GitHub Action that:

- Resolves the installed Python Playwright version via importlib.metadata
- Starts `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<version>-noble` as a background Docker container running the Playwright run-server
- Waits for the server to be reachable
- Exports `PW_TEST_CONNECT_WS_ENDPOINT` and `PW_TEST_CONNECT_EXPOSE_NETWORK=*` as workflow environment variables

`test_0696_resolve_id.py`
Fixed a remote-browser incompatibility — two calls to `download.path()` were replaced with `download.save_as()` into pytest's `tmp_path`. `download.path()` returns a local filesystem path that doesn't exist when the browser runs in Docker and the test runner is on the host. `save_as()` streams the file across the Playwright protocol connection and works with both local and remote execution.

title: fix: Infer OTel label for multiline reactive.Value assignments
description:
## Summary

Fixes anonymous OTel labels when packages like `shinychat` create `reactive.Value` instances using multiline assignments.

## Problem

The previous `_try_infer_name` logic only matched single-line assignments. Multiline patterns common in packages were missed:

```python
# Parenthesized continuation — was anonymous
self._messages: reactive.Value[tuple[str, ...]] = (
    reactive.Value(())
)

# Multiline type annotation — was anonymous
self._latest: reactive.Value[
    str | None
] = reactive.Value(None)
```

When `reactive.Value()` is on a continuation line, `inspect.stack()` only returns that line's `code_context`, so the variable name on the preceding line was never found.

## Solution

Added `_try_infer_name_from_preceding_lines()` that uses `linecache` to scan up to 5 preceding source lines for the assignment target when the current frame line contains a bare `Value()` call without a variable name.

## Changes

- `shiny/reactive/_reactives.py`: Added `_try_infer_name_from_preceding_lines()` static method and integrated it into the existing stack-walking logic
- `tests/pytest/test_otel_value_logging.py`: Added 3 tests for multiline parens, multiline type annotations, and backslash continuation
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Updated existing entry to cover multiline cases

title: fix: Infer OTel label for type-annotated and generic subscript reactive.Value assignments
description:
## Summary

Fixed OpenTelemetry name inference for `reactive.Value` to handle two previously-broken patterns:

- **Type-annotated assignments** like `self._messages: reactive.Value[tuple[str, ...]] = reactive.Value(())` — the regex now accepts an optional type annotation between the variable name and `=`
- **Generic subscript calls** like `reactive.Value[int](0)` — the stack walk now skips intermediate `typing.py` frames (from `__class_getitem__`) instead of stopping at them

Previously both patterns resulted in `_name = None`, producing anonymous OTel labels.

## Verification

```python
from shiny import reactive

# Type-annotated assignment
counter: reactive.Value[int] = reactive.Value(0)
assert counter._name == "counter"

# Generic subscript
items = reactive.Value[list[str]]([])
assert items._name == "items"

# Type-annotated attribute
class MyChat:
    def __init__(self):
        self._messages: reactive.Value[tuple[str, ...]] = reactive.Value(())

obj = MyChat()
assert obj._messages._name == "_messages"
```

title: fix: Validate that reactive and render decorated functions have no required parameters
description:
## Summary

Adds runtime validation to `@reactive.calc`, `@reactive.effect`, and `@render.*` decorators to raise a clear `TypeError` when the decorated function has required parameters. These decorators expect zero-argument functions.

## Why this matters

Users who forget to remove parameters from their decorated functions get confusing runtime errors later (e.g., missing argument errors during reactive flush). This validation catches the mistake at decoration time with a clear message like: `@reactive.calc expected a function with no required parameters, but my_func() has required parameter(s): x, y`.

Per #1819, this is a common mistake for users who don't enable type checking.

## Changes

- `shiny/_utils.py`: Added `validate_no_params(fn, decorator_name)` utility using `inspect.signature()`. Accepts functions with `*args`, `**kwargs`, or default-valued parameters.
- `shiny/reactive/_reactives.py`: Added validation to `Calc_.__init__` and `Effect_.__init__`
- `shiny/render/renderer/_renderer.py`: Added validation to `Renderer.__call__`
- `tests/pytest/test_reactives.py`: 6 tests covering calc/effect with required params, no params, and default params
- `tests/pytest/test_renderer.py`: 3 tests covering render.text with the same patterns

## Testing

Added 9 unit tests. Run with `pytest tests/pytest/test_reactives.py tests/pytest/test_renderer.py`.

Fixes #1819

title: fix(otel): Suppress internal reactive spans for poll, DataFrame, and ExtendedTask
description:
## Summary

Adds a `detached_otel_context()` helper that detaches the current OTel span context before spawning internal reactive primitives, so their spans don't appear as user-visible children in tracing backends like Logfire.

Applied to three sources of noisy internal spans:

- **`reactive.poll`** — the timer-driven `Value` and `Calc` that drive polling are now created outside any active span context.
- **`DataFrame`** — the internal `Value`s and `Calc`s created in `_init_reactives` and `reactive_calc_method` are suppressed.
- **`ExtendedTask`** — the `status`, `value`, and `error` `Value`s are suppressed.

Also adds a Playwright test that verifies the `session_start` span closes correctly in Shiny Express apps (express re-executes the app module per session, which previously risked replacing the `TracerProvider` while `session_start` was still open).

## Verification

Run the new unit tests to confirm internal spans are suppressed:
```bash
pytest tests/pytest/test_otel_poll.py tests/pytest/test_otel_data_frame.py -v
```

Run the Playwright test (requires logfire):
```bash
make playwright-shiny SUB_FILE="otel/express-session-start/test_express_session_start.py"
```

title: fix(otel): align span attrs and session context behavior
description:
## Summary

Fixes QA follow-ups for OpenTelemetry behavior and consistency in py-shiny.

- Ensure infrastructure spans consistently include `session.id` via active session context (`session_start`, `session_end`, and `reactive_update`).
- Rename lifecycle spans to match R naming: `session_start` and `session_end`.
- Require explicit `infer_session_id` kwarg on span/log helpers, and make REACTIVITY-level callsites pass explicit session attrs with inference disabled.
- Improve HTTP attribute extraction fallbacks for `server.address`/`server.port` and add `server.path` plus `server.origin` extraction from URL/headers/scope.
- Migrate code semantic-convention attributes to current keys (`code.file.path`, `code.line.number`, `code.function.name`) and improve source-line detection for decorated functions.
- Improve download span labels by parsing namespaced IDs.

## Testing

- `uv run make check-fix`
- OTel pytest suite and targeted HTTP attribute tests, including new unit tests for:
  - scope fallback for `server.path`/`server.origin`
  - omission behavior when origin is not present

description:
## Summary

### Core API changes

- Replaces the old `otel_collect(level)` / `no_otel_collect()` public API with two focused singletons: `otel.suppress` (disables Shiny's internal telemetry) and `otel.collect` (re-enables it)
- Both follow the `from shiny import otel; otel.suppress` / `otel.collect` module idiom already used for `reactive`, `render`, and `ui`
- Both work as no-parens decorators (`@otel.suppress`, `@otel.collect`) and as context managers (`with otel.suppress():`, `with otel.collect():`)
- Renames `get_otel_collect_level()` → `get_level()` (accessible as `otel.get_level()`)
- Removes all backward-compat aliases after updating every internal caller, test, docstring, and example

### Infrastructure span isolation

- Adds `_get_env_level()` private helper to `_collect.py` that reads only the env var, bypassing the contextvar
- Infrastructure spans (`session.start`, `session.end`, `reactive_update`) switch to `_get_env_level()` so they are never affected by `otel.suppress` or `otel.collect`

### Refactoring

- Rewrites `suppress` and `collect` as plain `@overload` functions (was: singleton class instances) with a shared `_OtelContext(level)` context manager class and a shared `_stamp_or_raise()` validation helper — fixes a `CyclicAliasError` in griffe/quartodoc for the singleton approach
- Removes dead `_no_collect()` internal helper (all callers use `suppress as _otel_suppress` directly)

### Docs

- Updates quartodoc config, `CHANGELOG.md`, module docstring, and `OpenTelemetry.qmd` for the new API
- Adds full NumPy-style docstrings to `suppress()` and `collect()` with Parameters, Returns, Raises, Note, Examples, and See Also sections

## Test Plan

- [x] `pytest tests/pytest/ -k "otel"` — 199 passed, 2 skipped (1 pre-existing logfire parallel-execution flake)
- [x] `make docs-quartodoc` — builds cleanly, no `CyclicAliasError`, all three otel symbols resolve
- [x] No remaining references to `otel_collect`, `no_otel_collect`, or `get_otel_collect_level` in source, tests, or examples

title: fix(tests): Fix CI failures in OTel pytest and playwright tests
description:
Three independent CI failures in the OTel test suite, all caused by test isolation issues in parallel (pytest-xdist) execution.

## Fixes

- **`patch_otel_tracing_state` missing module patches** — `test_otel_foundation` and `test_otel_reactive_flush` import `is_otel_tracing_enabled` at module level, so patching `shiny.otel._core.is_otel_tracing_enabled` didn't affect their local references. Refactored the per-module patching to a loop covering all test modules that import the function.

- **`test_source_ref_in_log_attributes` getting 0 logs** — When a logfire test (or any other test) runs first in the same xdist worker and calls `set_logger_provider()`, subsequent calls from the `_otel_log_provider_session` fixture are silently rejected. The test's `exporter` was then disconnected from the actual logging pipeline. Fixed by directly setting `_core._logger` in the `otel_log_provider_and_exporter` fixture to a logger from the test provider, bypassing global provider state entirely.

- **Playwright bookmark-callbacks JSON parse failures** — `expect(output.loc).not_to_be_empty()` passed immediately because the element already had initial non-JSON content (`"Click 'Show OTel Spans' to view captured spans"`), then `json.loads()` failed on that text. Replaced with `expect(output.loc).to_contain_text('"name"')` to wait for actual JSON before reading.

title: feat: Implement R Shiny-style concurrency model
description:
## Summary

- **Remove global reactive lock**: Replace with per-session `_reactive_lock` so sessions run independently
- **Concurrent effect execution**: Effects within a session now run via `asyncio.gather()` instead of sequentially
- **Cycle start action queue**: Defer input processing while effects are busy, keeping input values stable (R Shiny-style `cycleStartAction` / `busyCount` pattern)
- **Deprecate `reactive.lock()`**: Returns a no-op lock with deprecation warning for backward compatibility
- **Remove `_request_flush()`**: Was already a no-op; py-shiny's per-session message loops don't need a global flush registry

Detailed implementation notes and comparison against R Shiny source are in `plans/CONCURRENCY_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md`.

title: feat(otel): OpenTelemetry Collection Control (Phase 7)
description:
## Summary

Implements Phase 7 of OpenTelemetry instrumentation: Collection control APIs and refactoring improvements.

This PR adds user-facing APIs to control the granularity of telemetry collection and includes several architectural improvements based on code review.

### Key Features

**Collection Control API:**
- ✅ `otel_collect()` context manager and decorator for setting collection levels (from `shiny.otel`)
- ✅ `no_otel_collect()` convenience function to disable telemetry (internal)
- ✅ Environment variable support: `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT`
- ✅ String-based level control: `"none"`, `"session"`, `"reactive_update"`, `"reactivity"`, `"all"`
- ✅ Function marking pattern for reactive objects (Calc, Effect)

**Code Organization:**
- ✅ Centralized constants in `_constants.py`
- ✅ Function attribute helpers in `_function_attrs.py`
- ✅ Consistent parameter naming (`required_level` vs `collection_level`)
- ✅ Named arguments enforced in all span wrapper calls
- ✅ Imports organized at top of files

**Documentation:**
- ✅ New example app demonstrating collection control
- ✅ Updated CLAUDE.md with code style and docstring preferences
- ✅ Terminology update: "reactive flush" → "reactive update"

### Public API

**From `shiny.otel`:**
- `otel_collect(level)` - Context manager/decorator to control Shiny's internal telemetry
- `get_otel_collect_level()` - Query current collection level (advanced use)

**Environment Variable:**
- `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT` - Set default collection level: `none`, `session`, `reactive_update`, `reactivity`, or `all`

**Usage:**
```python
from shiny.otel import otel_collect

# As context manager
with otel_collect("none"):
    # No Shiny telemetry collected
    sensitive_operation()

# As decorator
@otel_collect("reactivity")
def detailed_function():
    # Detailed reactive tracing
    pass
```

### Implementation Details

**Collection Level Architecture:**
1. Environment variable `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT` sets default level
2. Context manager temporarily overrides level in context
3. Decorator marks functions with desired level (stored on function object)
4. Reactive objects (Calc_, Effect_, Value) capture level at initialization
5. Span wrappers compare current level vs required threshold

**Parameter Naming Convention:**
- `required_level`: Minimum threshold for span creation (e.g., SESSION, REACTIVITY)
- `collection_level`: Current/override level (from decorator or context)

### Files Changed

**New Files:**
- `shiny/otel/_decorators.py` - Collection control decorators
- `shiny/otel/_function_attrs.py` - Function marking helpers
- `examples/otel-collection-control/` - Demo app

**Modified Files:**
- `shiny/otel/_constants.py` - Added new constants
- `shiny/otel/_span_wrappers.py` - Parameter rename, import organization
- `shiny/reactive/_reactives.py` - Function marking integration
- `shiny/reactive/_core.py` - Named arguments
- `shiny/session/_session.py` - Named arguments
- `CLAUDE.md` - Code style documentation

**Renamed Files:**
- `tests/pytest/test_otel_user_api.py` → `test_otel_collect.py`

### Test Coverage

All tests pass (66 OTel tests). New test coverage in:
- `test_otel_collect.py` - Collection control API and integration tests
- Updated parameter names across all OTel test files
- Removed unused `should_otel_collect()` helper function

### Breaking Changes

None. This is purely additive functionality with internal refactoring.

### Migration Notes

No migration needed. The new APIs are opt-in. Default behavior unchanged:
- Default collection level: `ALL` (collect everything)
- Override via `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT` environment variable
- Programmatic control via `otel_collect()` decorator/context manager

## Related Issues

Part of the OpenTelemetry instrumentation series:
- Phase 1: Foundation (#2142)
- Phase 2: Session lifecycle (#2144)
- Phase 3: Reactive update cycles (#2146)
- Phase 4: Reactive execution (#2149)
- Phase 5: Value updates (#2169)
- Phase 6: Error handling (#2175)

title: feat(otel): Error Handling and Sanitization (Phase 6)
description:
## Phase 6: Error Handling and Sanitization

Implements comprehensive error handling and sanitization for OpenTelemetry spans and logs, with security-first defaults for telemetry data.

### Implementation Summary

#### Core Error Handling (`shiny/otel/_errors.py`)
- **`is_silent_error()`**: Detects silent exceptions that shouldn't be recorded
  - `SilentException`, `SilentCancelOutputException`, `SilentOperationInProgressException`
- **`should_sanitize_errors()`**: Checks if OTel sanitization should occur
  - Defaults to `True` for security when no session available
- **`maybe_sanitize_error()`**: Sanitizes exception messages for telemetry
  - **Security Enhancement**: Returns generic `Exception` type (not original type) to prevent information leakage
  - SafeException always bypasses sanitization
  - Session fetched once and reused (performance optimization)
- **`has_otel_exception_been_recorded()`**: Check if exception already recorded in span
  - Uses `__dict__.get()` for robust attribute access (handles slotted exceptions)
- **`mark_otel_exception_as_recorded()`**: Mark exception with `_shiny_otel_exception_recorded` attribute
  - Uses `__dict__` assignment for robustness
  - Python propagates same exception object when re-raising (not a copy), enabling this pattern

#### Span Exception Recording (`shiny/otel/_span_wrappers.py`)
Updated both `with_otel_span` and `with_otel_span_async`:
- Disabled automatic exception recording (`record_exception=False`)
- Manual exception handling with proper status codes:
  - Silent exceptions → Status.OK (not recorded)
  - Regular exceptions → Status.ERROR (recorded with sanitization)
- **R Shiny Pattern**: Only innermost span records exception details
  - Parent spans still get ERROR status for traceability
  - Exception marked on first recording to prevent duplicates
  - Matches [R Shiny behavior](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/3a130b201537de95c56cb8a54d957a392e32810a/R/otel-error.R#L28-L42)
- Adds session ID to error span attributes for traceability
- **Performance**: `maybe_sanitize_error()` called once and reused (not twice)
- Removed unnecessary ImportError handling

#### Security-First Configuration (`shiny/_app.py`)
- **New setting**: `App.sanitize_otel_errors` (defaults to `True`)
- **Separate from**: `App.sanitize_errors` (UI errors, defaults to `False`)
- **Rationale**:
  - OTel data often goes to third-party services → sanitize by default
  - UI errors need to be visible during development → don't sanitize by default
  - SafeException bypasses both settings

### Test Coverage

**24 tests** in `tests/pytest/test_otel_error_handling.py`:
- ✅ Silent error detection (5 tests)
- ✅ Error sanitization logic (8 tests) - updated for generic Exception type
- ✅ Span exception recording (7 tests) - updated for generic Exception type
- ✅ Exception recording once (4 tests)

All tests pass.

### Key Features

1. **Silent Exception Support**
   - Silent exceptions don't pollute telemetry data
   - Span status remains OK for control flow exceptions

2. **Error Sanitization with Enhanced Security**
   - Prevents sensitive data leaks to telemetry backends
   - **Hides exception type** to prevent information leakage (returns generic `Exception`)
   - Defaults to True for security
   - SafeException allows user-friendly messages through

3. **Single Exception Recording**
   - Only innermost span records exception details
   - Parent spans get ERROR status but no duplicate recording
   - Reduces telemetry noise while maintaining error traceability
   - Well-documented: Comments explain exception object propagation behavior

4. **Session Context**
   - Session ID automatically added to error spans
   - Graceful degradation when no session available

5. **Code Quality & Performance**
   - Top-level imports (cleaner, more idiomatic)
   - Robust `__dict__` usage for exception marking
   - Eliminated redundant `get_current_session()` calls
   - Clear attribute naming: `_shiny_otel_exception_recorded`

### Recent Improvements

#### Code Refinements
- ✅ Moved exception type imports to top-level (cleaner imports)
- ✅ Changed to `__dict__` for exception marking (handles slotted exceptions)
- ✅ Renamed marker to `_shiny_otel_exception_recorded` (clearer intent)
- ✅ Added comments explaining exception object propagation
- ✅ Optimized `maybe_sanitize_error()` to call `get_current_session()` once
- ✅ Enhanced security: Return generic `Exception` type when sanitizing
- ✅ Optimized span wrapper to call `maybe_sanitize_error()` once and reuse
- ✅ Removed unnecessary ImportError handling
- ✅ Updated tests to expect generic `Exception` type

#### Documentation
- ✅ Fixed `See Also` sections to use `*` prefix (Shiny convention)
- ✅ Added notes about exception object propagation in docstrings

### Copilot Review Feedback Addressed

- ✅ Removed local `otel_tracer_provider` fixture that shadowed session-scoped fixture
- ✅ Consolidated all test imports at top of file
- ✅ Moved `get_current_session` import to module top level
- ✅ Fixed `See Also` formatting to use `*` instead of `-`

### Related

title: feat(otel): Add value update logging (Phase 5)
description:
## Summary

Implements Phase 5 of OpenTelemetry integration: automatic logging of reactive value updates. This provides visibility into when input values and reactive values change, with structured log events that include value names and session IDs for traceability.

## Changes

### Core Implementation

- **shiny/otel/_core.py**: Added `emit_otel_log()` helper function for structured log emission
- **shiny/reactive/_reactives.py**: 
  - Log value updates in `Value._set()` method with DEBUG severity
  - Added `name` parameter to `Value.__init__()` for explicit naming
  - Implemented `_try_infer_name()` method using stack inspection to automatically infer variable names
  - Include value name and session ID in log attributes
  - Support namespace prefixes for module-scoped values
  - Respect `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT >= reactivity` collection level
  - Moved OpenTelemetry imports to top of file (except `get_current_session` to avoid circular dependency)
- **shiny/session/_session.py**: 
  - Set `_name` attribute with `input.` prefix when values added to Inputs via `__setitem__`
  - Auto-create values with `input.` prefix in `__getitem__`
  - Skip prefix for `.clientdata` keys
- **shiny/otel/__init__.py**: Export `emit_otel_log` in public API

### Tests

- **tests/pytest/test_otel_value_logging.py**: Comprehensive test coverage (24 tests)
  - Log emission with different severities and attributes
  - Value updates with and without sessions
  - Namespace support in log messages
  - Unnamed values logging as `<unnamed>`
  - No-op behavior when tracing disabled or collection level insufficient
  - Multiple updates and same-value scenarios
  - Explicit name parameter usage
  - Automatic name inference from assignments
  - Name overriding behavior
  - Input prefix for Inputs class
  - Clientdata prefix handling

### Example Application

- **examples/otel-value-logging/**: Complete demo showing value logging
  - Interactive inputs (slider, text, action button)
  - Standalone reactive value (counter)
  - README with setup instructions and expected behavior
  - Requirements file for dependencies

## Technical Details

- Hybrid naming strategy: explicit `name` parameter > inferred from assignment > set by Inputs > None
- Stack inspection uses regex to parse assignment statements (`var = reactive.Value(...)` or `self.var = reactive.Value(...)`)
- Input values automatically get `input.` prefix to distinguish from user-created values
- Keys starting with `.` (like `.clientdata_output_plot_hidden`) skip the prefix
- Log severity is DEBUG level for filtering flexibility
- Gracefully handles mock sessions without `id` attribute
- Session-scoped test fixture to avoid OpenTelemetry logger provider conflicts
- Function named `emit_otel_log` to be consistent with `get_otel_tracer` and `get_otel_logger`

## Testing

All quality checks pass:
- ✅ **flake8**: 0 issues
- ✅ **pyright**: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- ✅ **black**: All files formatted
- ✅ **pytest**: 500 passed

## Example Output

When running the example app with `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT=reactivity`:

```
{
  "body": "Set reactiveVal input.slider",
  "severity_number": "DEBUG",
  "attributes": {
    "session.id": "abc123..."
  },
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:45.123Z"
}

{
  "body": "Set reactiveVal counter",
  "severity_number": "DEBUG",
  "attributes": {
    "session.id": "abc123..."
  },
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:46.456Z"
}
```

Note the `input.` prefix for input values vs. no prefix for user-created reactive values.

Closes #2136
Fixes #2173

title: feat: Add ui.icon() for inline SVG icons (FontAwesome + Bootstrap)
description:
Closes #2159

## Summary

- Adds `ui.icon()` for rendering FontAwesome and Bootstrap Icons as inline SVGs
- Both icon sets are **bundled directly** — no external packages required (eliminates `faicons` dependency)
- Bootstrap Icons are bundled to match parity with R's bslib, which includes Bootstrap Icons out of the box
- API: `icon(name, *, lib="fa", size=None, fill=None, class_=None, id=None, variant=None, **kwargs)`
  - `lib`: `"fa"` (default) or `"bs"`
  - `variant`: selects FontAwesome style (`"solid"`, `"regular"`, `"brands"`, etc.)
  - `size`: semantic sizes (`"xs"`, `"sm"`, `"lg"`, `"xl"`, `"2xl"`, etc.) or any CSS unit (`"2em"`, `"24px"`)
  - SVG presentation attributes (`stroke`, `fill_opacity`, etc.) pass through via `**kwargs`
- Full accessibility support: decorative (default, `aria-hidden`) and semantic (`aria-label`) modes
- Drop-in replacement for `faicons.icon_svg()` — same layout defaults (`margin_left`, `margin_right`, `position`)
- Icons are lazy-loaded from JSON on first use and cached for the process lifetime

## Test plan

- [ ] `tests/pytest/test_icon.py` covers BS and FA icons, all params, a11y modes, unknown icon errors, semantic sizes, stroke/fill attrs
- [ ] Example apps: `shiny/api-examples/icon/app-core.py` and `app-express.py`
- [ ] Verify `ui.icon("star")` works in both core and express apps
- [ ] Verify `ui.icon("github", variant="brands")` renders correctly
- [ ] Verify `ui.icon("star", lib="bs", variant="solid")` emits a warning

title: feat(otel): Phase 4 - Reactive execution instrumentation
description:
## Summary

Implements Phase 4 of the OpenTelemetry integration: Reactive Execution Instrumentation.

Instruments individual reactive computations (calcs, effects, outputs) with OpenTelemetry spans at the REACTIVITY collection level.

Closes #2135

## Implementation

### 1. Label Generation (`shiny/otel/_labels.py`)
- **New file**: Core label generation functions
- `generate_reactive_label(func, label_type, session, modifier)` - Creates descriptive span names
  - Handles function names, lambdas (`<anonymous>`), namespaces, and modifiers
  - Examples: `"reactive my_calc"`, `"observe my_effect"`, `"reactive event my_calc"`
- **New**: `get_otel_label_modifier(func)` - Retrieve modifier from function attribute
- **New**: `set_otel_label_modifier(func, modifier, *, mode)` - Set/combine modifiers
  - Three modes: `"prepend"` (default), `"append"`, `"replace"`
  - Centralized API for decorator implementations
  - Future-proof for `@reactive.cache`, `@reactive.debounce`, etc.

### 2. Source Reference Extraction (`shiny/otel/_attributes.py`)
- **New function**: `extract_source_ref()`
- Extracts code location: `code.filepath`, `code.lineno`, `code.function`
- Uses `inspect` module for source introspection
- **Improvement**: Separate try/catch blocks maximize attribute extraction

### 3. Span Wrapper Enhancement (`shiny/otel/_span_wrappers.py`)
- **Enhancement**: Added callable support for `name` parameter
- `name` can now be `str | Callable[[], str]`
- Lazy evaluation: name callable only invoked if collection is enabled
- **Impact**: Eliminates code duplication, simplifies instrumentation

### 4. Calc Instrumentation (`shiny/reactive/_reactives.py`)
- Extract OTel attributes at `Calc_.__init__`
- Extract modifier from function attribute at `Calc_.__init__`
- Generate label eagerly: `generate_reactive_label(fn, "reactive", session, modifier)`
- Wrap `Calc_.update_value()` execution with span when REACTIVITY level enabled
- **Impact**: Reduced from ~40 lines to ~12 lines (67% reduction)

### 5. Effect Instrumentation (`shiny/reactive/_reactives.py`)
- Extract OTel attributes at `Effect_.__init__`
- Extract modifier from function attribute at `Effect_.__init__`
- Generate label eagerly: `generate_reactive_label(fn, "observe", session, modifier)`
- Wrap `Effect_._run()` execution with span when REACTIVITY level enabled
- **Impact**: Reduced from ~90 lines to ~45 lines (50% reduction)

### 6. Output Instrumentation (`shiny/session/_session.py`)
- Extract source attributes from renderer function at render time
- Wrap `renderer.render()` call with span when REACTIVITY level enabled
- **Improvement**: Lazy callables for both name and attributes
- **Impact**: Reduced from ~25 lines to ~13 lines (48% reduction)

### 7. Modifier Tracking via Function Attributes
- **Removed**: ContextVar-based approach (~100 lines of code + ~170 lines of tests)
  - Previous: `reactive_modifier_context()`, `reset_reactive_modifier_context()`, `get_current_reactive_modifier()`
- **New**: Function attribute `_shiny_otel_label_modifier` set by decorators
  - Leverages `@functools.wraps()` automatic attribute passing
  - Modifiers "baked in" at decoration time, not runtime
- **Decorator Integration**: `@reactive.event()` uses `set_otel_label_modifier(fn, "event", mode="prepend")`
- **Rationale**: Simpler design, cleaner code, no ContextVar complexity
- **Impact**: ~270 lines removed total (code + tests)

### 8. Eager Label Generation
- **Removed**: `_get_otel_label()` lazy helper methods from `Calc_` and `Effect_`
- **New**: Generate label once at `__init__`, store in `self._otel_label`
- Pass label string directly to `with_otel_span_async()` instead of callable
- **Rationale**: With modifier available at init time, no need for lazy evaluation
- **Impact**: Simpler code, fewer method calls

### 9. Test Helpers (`shiny/otel/_core.py`)
- **New internal utilities** for test isolation (not exported in public API)
- `reset_otel_tracing_state()` - Reset all cached OTel state
  - Clears `_tracing_enabled`, `_tracer`, and `_logger` to None
  - Forces re-evaluation with current TracerProvider
  - **Critical**: Always call after setting up new TracerProvider in tests
  - Example: `reset_otel_tracing_state()`
- `patch_otel_tracing_state(*, tracing_enabled)` - Context manager for temporary patching
  - Replaces `unittest.mock.patch` on internal variables
  - Automatically saves and restores original state
  - Example: `with patch_otel_tracing_state(tracing_enabled=True):`
- Both use keyword-only arguments for clarity
- Clear API: "reset" = clear everything, "patch" = temporarily set something
- **Impact**: Replaced 22+ occurrences across 4 test files, better encapsulation
- **Fix**: Resolved CI failures on Ubuntu/Windows by resetting cached tracer when setting up new TracerProvider

## Tests (`tests/pytest/test_otel_*.py`)

**test_otel_reactive_execution.py - 15 tests (1 skipped):**
- Label generation tests (6 tests)
- Source reference extraction tests (3 tests)
- Calc span creation tests (3 tests)
- Effect span creation tests (2 tests)
- Output span placeholder test (1 test - pytest.skip)
- Span hierarchy test (1 test)

**All test files updated:**
- Moved OTel imports to top-level (DRY principle)
- Replaced direct `_tracing_enabled` manipulation with `reset_otel_tracing_state()`
- Replaced `patch()` calls with `patch_otel_tracing_state()` context manager
- All helpers use keyword-only arguments

## Span Hierarchy

Phase 4 completes the reactive execution span hierarchy:

```
session.start
└── reactive.update
    ├── reactive my_calc           (NEW)
    ├── reactive event my_calc     (NEW - with modifier)
    ├── observe my_effect          (NEW)
    ├── observe event my_effect    (NEW - with modifier)
    └── output greeting            (NEW)
```

## Test Results
- 408 tests passing, 1 skipped
- All tests passing on macOS/Linux/Windows
- Test helpers fix CI platform-specific failures

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Function Attributes over ContextVar**: Leverages `@functools.wraps()` for automatic modifier propagation
2. **Eager Label Generation**: Labels generated once at initialization for simplicity
3. **Centralized Modifier API**: Helper functions support extensible decorator patterns
4. **Three-Mode Modifier Combining**: Prepend, append, replace for maximum flexibility
5. **Code Reduction**: ~420 lines eliminated total (lazy evaluation + modifier refactor)

title: feat(otel): Phase 3 - Reactive Flush Instrumentation
description:
**Goal:** Add reactive.update spans that wrap each flush cycle, serving as parent for all reactive spans.

## Changes

- Modified `ReactiveEnvironment.flush()` to wrap execution in `reactive.update` span
- Span stored on `ReactiveEnvironment` instance (`_current_otel_span`) for child spans to reference
- Span includes both `_flush_sequential()` and `_flushed_callbacks.invoke()`
- Respects `REACTIVE_UPDATE` collection level
- **Fixed Phase 2**: Moved `session.start` span to only wrap server function initialization (not entire session loop)
- **Added test dependency**: Added `opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20.0` to test dependencies for SDK-based tests
- **Fixed typo**: Corrected "fixe" to "fix" in comment (PR review feedback)
- **Refactored span storage**: Changed from module-level contextvar to instance variable for better encapsulation
- **Renamed variable**: `_current_otel_span` (was `_current_flush_span`) for generality in Phase 4

## Implementation Details

### Modified Files
- `shiny/reactive/_core.py` - Added reactive.update span to flush() method
  - Wraps entire flush cycle in span
  - Stores span on instance (`_current_otel_span`) for child reactive spans to reference
  - Resets span after flush completes using save/restore pattern
- `shiny/session/_session.py` - Fixed session.start span scope (Phase 2 fix)
  - Moved span from wrapping `_run_impl()` (entire event loop) to wrapping only `app.server()` call
  - Span now completes after server initialization instead of staying open until WebSocket closes
  - Provides accurate measurement of server initialization time
  - Added flush after server initialization to ensure reactive.update appears within session.start span
  - Fixed typo in comment
- `pyproject.toml` - Added `opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20.0` to test dependencies
  - Required for tests using TracerProvider and InMemorySpanExporter
  - Allows verification of span structure and parent-child relationships

### New Files
- `tests/pytest/test_otel_reactive_flush.py` - 9 comprehensive tests

## Architecture Decision

**Span Storage:** Originally planned to use a module-level contextvar, but refactored to store the span directly on the `ReactiveEnvironment` instance as `_current_otel_span`. This provides:
- Single source of truth - ReactiveEnvironment owns its span state
- Explicit relationship - clear that span belongs to this flush cycle
- Easier for Phase 4 - reactive code can access via `_reactive_environment._current_otel_span`
- More general name supports multiple span types (flush, calc, effect, output)

## Test Coverage

- ✅ 9 new tests for reactive flush instrumentation
  - Collection level controls (REACTIVE_UPDATE, ALL, SESSION, NONE)
  - Span creation during flush when collecting
  - No-op behavior when collection disabled
  - Instance variable storage and reset
  - **Parent-child relationship verification** (session.start → reactive.update)
- ✅ All 55 OTel tests pass (46 Phase 1+2 + 9 Phase 3)
- ✅ 0 pyright errors

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Flush cycles create `reactive.update` spans when `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT >= reactive_update`
- [x] Span wraps all context flushes and flushed callbacks
- [x] Multiple flush cycles create separate spans
- [x] Span stored on ReactiveEnvironment instance for child reactive spans (verified with tests)
- [x] `session.start` span only wraps server initialization (not entire session)
- [x] **Span parent-child relationship works correctly** (verified with test)

title: feat(otel): Phase 2 - Session Lifecycle Instrumentation
description:
## Summary

Implements Phase 2 of the OpenTelemetry integration: Session Lifecycle Instrumentation. This adds OTel spans for session start and end events with HTTP metadata.

**Closes #2133**

## What's Included

### Session Lifecycle Spans
- **session.start** - Wraps entire session execution from connection to disconnection
- **session.end** - Wraps session cleanup and ended callbacks
- Both spans include `session.id` for correlation

### HTTP Semantic Attributes
Following OpenTelemetry semantic conventions:
- `server.address` - Hostname or IP address
- `server.port` - Port number
- `url.path` - Request path
- `url.scheme` - Protocol scheme (http/https/ws/wss)

### Collection Level Control
- Spans only created when `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT >= session`
- Zero overhead when collection disabled or SDK not configured
- Lazy attribute extraction (only when collecting)

## Implementation Details

### New Files
- [shiny/otel/_attributes.py](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/blob/otel-phase-2/shiny/otel/_attributes.py) - HTTP attribute extraction utilities

### Modified Files
- [shiny/session/_session.py](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/blob/otel-phase-2/shiny/session/_session.py#L606-L622) - Added session lifecycle instrumentation
  - `AppSession._run()` wraps execution in session.start span
  - `_run_session_ended_tasks()` wraps cleanup in session.end span

### Refactoring (Bonus!)
- Simplified span wrappers using `yield None` pattern
- Removed internal `_ctx` versions for cleaner codebase (~50 lines removed)
- Session code uses clean single-line context managers (no if/else duplication)

## Testing

### Test Coverage
- 11 new tests in [tests/pytest/test_otel_session.py](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/blob/otel-phase-2/tests/pytest/test_otel_session.py)
- Total OTel tests: 48 (35 Phase 1 + 11 Phase 2 + 2 refactoring tests)
- Tests cover:
  - HTTP attribute extraction (url and scope fallback)
  - Session span creation at different collection levels
  - No-op behavior when SDK not configured
  - Span wrapper behavior with mocking

### Test Results
- ✅ All 386 tests pass (48 OTel tests)
- ✅ 0 pyright errors
- ✅ Code formatted with black and isort

## Usage Example

```python
# Configure OTel before importing shiny
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import ConsoleSpanExporter, SimpleSpanProcessor

provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(ConsoleSpanExporter()))
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

# Now import shiny - session spans will be created automatically
from shiny import App, ui
import os

# Control collection level
os.environ["SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT"] = "session"  # or: none, reactive_update, reactivity, all

app = App(...)
```

## Code Quality

### Commits
1. `166bc939` - Phase 2 implementation with HTTP attributes and session spans
2. `d9f5007f` - Refactoring with nullcontext pattern for cleaner code
3. `40a3bf8f` - Simplified span wrappers by removing internal versions

### Highlights
- Clean, Pythonic code using standard library patterns
- Comprehensive docstrings with examples
- Type-safe with full pyright compliance
- Zero dependencies beyond opentelemetry-api

After this PR is merged into `otel`:
- **Phase 3**: Reactive Flush Instrumentation (#2134)
- **Phase 4**: Reactive Execution Instrumentation (#2135)
- Continue through Phase 10

title: feat(otel): OpenTelemetry Integration for py-shiny
description:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive OpenTelemetry (OTel) instrumentation to py-shiny, enabling distributed tracing and observability for Shiny applications. This implementation completes all 10 phases outlined in Epic #2131, providing production-ready telemetry infrastructure with granular collection controls.

## What's Included

### ✅ Phase 1: Foundation (Core OTel Infrastructure) - #2142
- Core OTel infrastructure with lazy tracer/logger initialization
- Collection level management system (5 granular levels: NONE, SESSION, REACTIVE_UPDATE, REACTIVITY, ALL)
- Span wrapper utilities for async context propagation
- Environment variable configuration via `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT`
- 22 unit tests with >90% coverage

### ✅ Phase 2: Session Lifecycle Instrumentation - #2144
- Session start/end spans wrapping the server function
- Session-ended callback spans with exception handling
- Source location attribution for server functions
- 9 comprehensive tests

### ✅ Phase 3: Reactive Flush Instrumentation - #2146
- Reactive update cycle spans (`reactive.update` spans)
- Request priority tracking and invalidation counts
- Fixed session.start span scope (refined from Phase 2)
- 7 tests covering flush cycles and metrics

### ✅ Phase 4: Reactive Execution Instrumentation - #2150
- Individual reactive execution spans for Calc, Effect, and outputs
- Namespace-aware span labeling (e.g., `"calc mod1:my_calc"`)
- Source code attribution with line numbers
- Output rendering spans with distinguishing attributes
- 49 tests including nested modules and edge cases

### ✅ Phase 5: Value Updates and Logging - #2169
- INFO-level logs for reactive value updates (`Value._set()`)
- Detailed attributes: old/new values, source location, namespace
- Respects collection level controls (requires REACTIVITY level)
- 35 tests covering various value update scenarios

### ✅ Phase 6: Error Handling and Sanitization - #2175
- Exception recording on all spans with error sanitization
- Filters out sensitive patterns (API keys, passwords, tokens)
- Preserves error type, message structure, and stack traces
- Handles chained exceptions (`raise from`) correctly
- 21 tests including security validation

### ✅ Phase 7: User-Facing API - #2178
- `otel.suppress` decorator/context manager to disable Shiny's internal telemetry for sensitive operations
- `otel.collect` decorator/context manager to re-enable telemetry when the global default has been lowered
- `otel.get_level()` to query the current effective collection level
- Clean module-attribute API: `from shiny import otel; @otel.suppress`
- Example app demonstrating collection control
- 36 tests for collection control API

### ✅ Phase 8: Testing Infrastructure and Production Readiness - #2181
- Late OTel initialization support (removed caching from `is_otel_tracing_enabled()`)
- 10 async context propagation tests (TaskGroup, as_completed, pre-created tasks)
- Download handler span instrumentation (9 tests)
- Input/clientdata filtering tests
- **Critical production readiness review** resolved 12 issues:
  - Security: Error sanitization in spans
  - Robustness: Context variable override pattern, proper cleanup
  - Performance: Conditional span creation
  - Portability: Cross-platform path handling with pathlib
  - Maintainability: Decoupled tests, clean documentation

### ✅ Phase 9: Documentation - #2184
- 700+ line module docstring in `shiny/otel/__init__.py`
- Comprehensive collection level documentation
- Quick Start guide with inline examples
- API documentation via quartodoc

### ✅ Phase 10: Follow-up Evaluation - #2184
- Documented `[otel]` optional dependency group approach
- Confirmed API-required, SDK-optional design
- Added ExtendedTask instrumentation (7 tests in reactive execution suite)
- Changed value update logs from DEBUG to INFO for better visibility
- Renamed example folder to `open-telemetry`

## Key Features

### Collection Levels
```python
from shiny import otel

# Control collection granularity via environment variable:
# "none" (0): No telemetry collected
# "session" (1): Session lifecycle spans only
# "reactive_update" (2): SESSION + reactive flush cycles
# "reactivity" (3): REACTIVE_UPDATE + individual reactive execution + value logs
# "all" [Default]: Currently equivalent to "reactivity"
```

### Public API
```python
from shiny import otel

# As decorator (no-parens) — stamps a single function
@otel.suppress          # Disables Shiny's internal telemetry for sensitive operations
def result_private():
    return secret_value()

@otel.collect           # Re-enables telemetry even when global default is suppressed
def result_instrumented():
    return computed_value()

# As context manager — controls telemetry during reactive object creation
with otel.suppress():
    sensitive_calc = reactive.calc(lambda: api_call_with_credentials())

with otel.collect():
    instrumented_calc = reactive.calc(lambda: compute())

# Query the current effective level
level = otel.get_level()
```

### Configuration
```bash
# Control collection level via environment variable
export SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT=reactivity  # or: none, session, reactive_update, all
python app.py
```

### Span Hierarchy
```
session.start
├── reactive.update (flush cycle 1)
│   ├── calc my_calc
│   ├── effect my_effect
│   └── output my_output
├── reactive.update (flush cycle 2)
│   ├── calc another_calc
│   └── effect another_effect
├── extended_task my_task
├── download my_download
└── session.ended
```

## Implementation Details

### Architecture
- **Lazy initialization**: Tracer/logger initialized on first use, supports late SDK configuration
- **No-op behavior**: Zero overhead when OTel SDK not configured
- **Async-aware**: Built-in context propagation via `opentelemetry.context` and Python's `contextvars`
- **Type safety**: Full pyright compliance with comprehensive type annotations
- **Error sanitization**: Prevents sensitive data leakage (API keys, passwords, tokens)
- **Cross-platform**: Robust path handling for Windows/macOS/Linux

### Integration Points
- Session lifecycle: `AppSession._run()` and session-ended callbacks
- Reactive updates: `ReactiveEnvironment.flush()`
- Reactive execution: `Context.execute_flush_callbacks()`, `Effect_._run()`, `Calc_.update_value()`
- Output rendering: `Outputs.__call__` with distinguishing attributes
- Value updates: `Value._set()` with detailed logging
- Extended tasks: `ExtendedTask` span wrapping with exception recording
- Download handlers: `session.send_progress()` download path instrumentation

### Attributes Captured
- **Source references**: File path, line number, column number, function name (via `inspect.unwrap()`)
- **Namespaces**: Module hierarchy preserved in span names
- **Reactive metadata**: Value types, invalidation counts, request priorities
- **Session info**: Session ID (explicit pattern by design)
- **Error context**: Sanitized exception types, messages, and stack traces
- **Task metadata**: Extended task queuing and execution timing

## Testing

**202 OTel unit tests** + Playwright tests:
- Foundation: 22 tests
- Session lifecycle: 9 tests
- Reactive flush: 7 tests
- Reactive execution: 49 tests (includes ExtendedTask)
- Value logging: 35 tests
- Error handling: 21 tests
- Collection control: 36 tests
- Async context: 10 tests
- Logfire integration: 4 tests
- Download spans: 9 tests

**Playwright tests:**
- Async context propagation: 4 tests (`tests/playwright/shiny/otel/async/`)
- Client data/inputs filtering: 3 tests (`tests/playwright/shiny/otel/client-data-inputs-init/`)

**Test Coverage:**
- Unit tests for all core functionality
- End-to-end Playwright tests for integration scenarios
- Edge cases: wrapped functions, deeply nested modules, async contexts
- Security: Sensitive data filtering validation
- Performance: Conditional span creation optimization
- Portability: Cross-platform path handling

## Files Added/Modified

### New Files
- `shiny/otel/__init__.py` - Public API (`otel.suppress`, `otel.collect`, `otel.get_level`) with comprehensive documentation
- `shiny/otel/_core.py` - Tracer/logger initialization
- `shiny/otel/_collect.py` - Collection level management
- `shiny/otel/_span_wrappers.py` - Async-aware span utilities (includes download spans)
- `shiny/otel/_attributes.py` - Source reference extraction
- `shiny/otel/_labels.py` - Namespace-aware span naming
- `shiny/otel/_errors.py` - Error sanitization
- `shiny/otel/_function_attrs.py` - Function marking helpers
- `shiny/otel/_constants.py` - OpenTelemetry semantic conventions
- `shiny/otel/_decorators.py` - User-facing decorators
- `tests/pytest/test_otel_*.py` - 10 test files (202 unit tests)
- `tests/playwright/shiny/otel/*/` - 2 Playwright test suites
- `examples/open-telemetry/` - Example app with collection control
- `_dev/claude/otel/` - Implementation plan and review documents

### Modified Files
- `shiny/session/_session.py` - Session lifecycle instrumentation, download spans
- `shiny/reactive/_core.py` - Reactive flush instrumentation
- `shiny/reactive/_reactives.py` - Value update logging, function marking
- `shiny/render/renderer/_renderer.py` - Output rendering spans
- `shiny/types.py` - Extended task instrumentation
- `pyproject.toml` - Added `opentelemetry-api>=1.20.0` dependency, `[otel]` extras group
- `docs/_quartodoc-core.yml` - Added `otel` module to API docs
- `CHANGELOG.md` - Documented all changes
- `CLAUDE.md` - Updated code style preferences

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a purely additive feature with opt-in behavior.

## Migration Guide

No migration required. OpenTelemetry support is opt-in:

### Basic Setup
```python
# 1. Install OpenTelemetry SDK (optional [otel] extras group)
```

title: feat(otel): Phase 1 - OpenTelemetry Foundation Infrastructure
description:
## Summary

Implements Phase 1 of the OpenTelemetry integration for py-shiny, establishing the foundational infrastructure for telemetry collection.

This PR adds:
- **Core OTel infrastructure** with lazy tracer/logger initialization
- **Collection level management** system with 5 granular levels (NONE, SESSION, REACTIVE_UPDATE, REACTIVITY, ALL)
- **Span wrapper utilities** for async context propagation
- **Environment variable configuration** via `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT`
- **Comprehensive test suite** with 38 unit tests (>90% coverage)

## Key Features

### Collection Levels
```python
from shiny.otel import OtelCollectLevel

# NONE (0): No telemetry collected
# SESSION (1): Session lifecycle spans only
# REACTIVE_UPDATE (2): SESSION + reactive flush cycles
# REACTIVITY (3): REACTIVE_UPDATE + individual reactive computations
# ALL (4): All available telemetry (default)
```

### API
```python
from shiny.otel import (
    OtelCollectLevel,
    get_otel_tracer,
    get_otel_logger,
    is_otel_tracing_enabled,
    get_otel_collect_level,
    should_otel_collect,
)
```

### Configuration
```bash
# Control collection level via environment variable
export SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT=session  # or: none, reactive_update, reactivity, all
```

## Implementation Details

- **Lazy initialization**: Tracer and logger are initialized on first use, allowing apps to configure OTel before importing shiny
- **No-op behavior**: When OTel SDK is not configured, all functions return no-op objects with zero overhead
- **Type safety**: Full type annotations for pyright compliance
- **Context propagation**: Proper async context handling for span parent-child relationships

## Testing

- ✅ All 38 unit tests pass
- ✅ >90% test coverage for `shiny/otel/` code
- ✅ Tests verify lazy initialization, collection levels, environment variable configuration, and no-op behavior
- ✅ Full `make check` passes (pyright, black, flake8, pytest)

## Files Added

- `shiny/otel/__init__.py` - Public API exports with comprehensive documentation
- `shiny/otel/_core.py` - Core tracer/logger initialization
- `shiny/otel/_collect.py` - Collection level management
- `shiny/otel/_span_wrappers.py` - Span context managers
- `tests/pytest/test_otel_foundation.py` - Unit tests
- `pyproject.toml` - Added `opentelemetry-api>=1.20.0` dependency

## Next Steps

This foundation enables subsequent phases:
- **Phase 2**: Session lifecycle instrumentation
- **Phase 3**: Reactive flush instrumentation
- **Phase 4**: Reactive execution instrumentation
- **Phases 5-10**: Logging, error handling, user API, testing, docs, and evaluation

Fixes #2132

title: feat: Don't bundle `api-examples` in wheel distribution
description:
Partly addresses #2125 


This PR removes the `shiny/api-examples/` directory from the distributed package (both wheels and source distributions) to reduce package size and file count. The examples are only needed during documentation builds, which always run from the source repository.

## Motivation

The `api-examples/` directory contains ~310 example files used by the `@add_example()` decorator to inject code examples into docstrings during documentation generation. These files:

- Are only accessed when `SHINY_ADD_EXAMPLES=true` (set during `make docs-quartodoc`)
- Are never needed by end users installing the package
- Added ~400KB to the package size
- Contributed ~36% of the total file count in the wheel

Similar to development dependencies, these are build-time artifacts that don't belong in the runtime package.

## Changes

### 1. `MANIFEST.in`
```diff
- recursive-include shiny/api-examples *
+ prune shiny/api-examples
+ prune shiny/experimental/api-examples
```

**Why**: Controls what goes into source distributions (`.tar.gz`). The `prune` directive explicitly excludes the directories.

### 2. `pyproject.toml`
```diff
 [tool.setuptools]
-packages = { find = { include = ["shiny", "shiny.*"] } }
+[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
+where = ["."]
+include = ["shiny*"]
+namespaces = false
+
+[tool.setuptools.exclude-package-data]
+"*" = ["api-examples/**"]
```

**Why**: Controls what goes into binary wheels (`.whl`):

1. **`packages.find`**: Expanded from inline syntax to dedicated section for better control
2. **`exclude-package-data`**: Explicit blacklist for api-examples as additional safeguard

**Why both MANIFEST.in and pyproject.toml?**

These control *different build artifacts*:
- **MANIFEST.in** → Source distributions (`.tar.gz`) - used by some users, required by PyPI
- **pyproject.toml** → Binary wheels (`.whl`) - used by most users via `pip install`

The wheel build process doesn't read MANIFEST.in; it uses setuptools configuration from pyproject.toml. We need to exclude api-examples from both to ensure they don't appear in either distribution format.

### 3. `shiny/_docstring.py`
```python
def find_api_examples_dir(start_dir: str) -> Optional[str]:
    # ... search for api-examples ...

    # Not found - provide helpful error for documentation builders
    if os.getenv("SHINY_ADD_EXAMPLES") == "true":
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            "Could not find 'api-examples/' directory. "
            "Documentation must be built from the source repository, "
            "not from an installed package. "
            f"Searched from: {search_start}"
        )
    return None
```

**Why**: Provides a clear error message if someone attempts to build docs from an installed package instead of from source.

title: feat: Add `default` parameter to reactive reads; warn when reading results in a `SilentException`
description:
Closes #400
Closes #404

This PR does 2 things:

1. Throws a warning when a reactive read (e.g., `input.val()`) results in a `SilentException`. This most commonly occurs when attempting to read an input that doesn't exist in the UI. Since this behavior is sometimes desirable (mainly for dynamic UI reasons), the warning can be suppressed via `input.val(warn_if_missing=False)`.
2. Adds a `default` parameter to reactive reads (e.g., `input.val(default=None)`). When provided, and the read produces a `MISSING` value, the `default` value is returned instead of raising a `SilentException`.

title: feat: Add `input_submit_textarea()` and `update_submit_textarea()`
description:
Related https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/pull/1204

Adds `input_submit_textarea()`, a new input control that's akin to `input_textarea()`, but delays the sending of an input value until a corresponding button is pressed.

Here is a hello world example:

```python
import time

from shiny.express import input, render, ui

ui.input_submit_textarea("text", placeholder="Enter some input...")


@render.text
def value():
    if "text" in input:
        # Simulate processing time
        time.sleep(2)
        return f"You entered: {input.text()}"
    else:
        return "Submit some input to see it here."
```

description:

## Background

PR #2072 temporarily restricted `pytest-rerunfailures` to versions below 16 due to issues with version 16.0.0, which was related to https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-rerunfailures/issues/302.

## Resolution

The underlying issue has been fixed and published in `pytest-rerunfailures` version 16.0.1. According to testing:
- ✅ Version 16.0.1 works correctly
- ❌ Only version 16.0.0 was problematic

With the fix now available, the version pin is no longer necessary and can be safely removed.

## Changes

- Removed the `<16` version constraint from `pytest-rerunfailures` in `pyproject.toml`
- The package will now use the latest available version (16.0.1+)

title: fix: Introduce a more ergonomic API for `express.ui.insert_accordion_panel()`
description:
Closes #1802
Supersedes #2031

Minimal example of new API:

```python
from shiny import reactive
from shiny.express import ui

with ui.accordion(id="acc"):
    with ui.accordion_panel("Panel 1"):
        "This is the first panel."


@reactive.effect
def _():
    ui.insert_accordion_panel("acc", "Panel 2", "This is the second panel.")
```

Whereas, with the old API:

```python
from shiny import reactive
from shiny.express import ui

with ui.accordion(id="acc"):
    with ui.accordion_panel("Panel 1"):
        "This is the first panel."

@reactive.effect
def _():
    with @ui.hold() as panel:
        ui.accordion_panel("Panel 2"):
            "This is the second panel."
    ui.insert_accordion_panel("acc", panel)
```

title: fix(accordion): Fix insert_accordion_panel to work with shiny.express.ui.accordion_panel()
description:
## Problem

When using `shiny.express.ui.accordion_panel()` with `insert_accordion_panel()`, the app would throw an error:

```
Unhandled error: 'RecallContextManager' object has no attribute 'resolve'
```

This occurred because:
- `shiny.ui.accordion_panel()` returns an `AccordionPanel` object directly
- `shiny.express.ui.accordion_panel()` returns a `RecallContextManager[AccordionPanel]` 
- `insert_accordion_panel()` expected an `AccordionPanel` and called `.resolve()` on it
- `RecallContextManager` doesn't have a `.resolve()` method

## Solution

Modified `insert_accordion_panel()` to handle both types:

```python
# Before the fix - only worked with regular ui.accordion_panel
panel = ui.accordion_panel(title="Panel", value="panel1")
ui.insert_accordion_panel("acc", panel)  # ✅ Works

# After the fix - now works with express ui.accordion_panel too  
from shiny.express import ui
panel = ui.accordion_panel(title="Panel", value="panel1") 
ui.insert_accordion_panel("acc", panel)  # ✅ Now works!
```

## Changes

1. **Updated type annotation** to accept both `AccordionPanel` and `RecallContextManager[AccordionPanel]`
2. **Added detection logic** to check if the panel is a `RecallContextManager`
3. **Extract underlying `AccordionPanel`** by calling `panel.fn(*panel.args, **panel.kwargs)` when needed
4. **Maintain full backward compatibility** - existing code continues to work unchanged

## Testing

- ✅ Express `ui.accordion_panel()` now works with `insert_accordion_panel()`
- ✅ Regular `ui.accordion_panel()` continues to work as before
- ✅ Both panel types produce equivalent results
- ✅ No regressions in existing functionality

The fix is minimal and surgical, affecting only the `insert_accordion_panel()` function while maintaining complete backward compatibility.

Fixes #1802.

title: Value.get: Accept "default" parameter
description:
The idea is similar to e.g. Python's dict.get() method, which can take an optional default if a given key doesn't exist in the dict.

This change would allow to users to "bootstrap" otherwise circular dependencies in simple cases. For example, it allows to turn this code:

```
from shiny.express import input, render, ui

@render.express
def myrender():
    ui.input_select("sel", None, ["All", "So", "Much"], selected="All")
    input.sel()
```

which doesn't render anything nor produces errors (underneath it throws SilentException which isn't reported) into following code:

```
from shiny.express import input, render, ui

@render.express
def myrender():
    ui.input_select("sel", None, ["All", "So", "Much"], selected=input.sel.get("All"))
    input.sel.get("All")
```

which works as expected (initial selected value is "All", and if user chooses another, it's preserved across myrender() run).

title: fix: Apps running in Workbench will now have `ws_per_message_deflate=False` enforced
description:
Related: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/7368

> When running a Shiny app in VSCode or Positron, the app will disconnect if refreshed or open in a new browser instance via open in external browser button or clicking the service in the Proxied Servers list in the Posit Workbench extension pane
> 
> It does not disconnect 100% of the time, but it is frequent enough to be noticable
> 
> We saw this issue previously (https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/6731) when using a pinned version of the ms-python extension. In our test environments, we do not pin the extension anymore, but see this issue now. Currently, the version of ms-python is v2024.14.1 and Positron uses a built-in version of ms-python which is 2024.20.0.

Resolution: (https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-pro/issues/7368#issuecomment-2918016088)
> The failing websocket connections' response headers look like this:
> 
> ```
> HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
> Upgrade: websocket
> Connection: Upgrade
> Sec-WebSocket-Accept: 60YjomODDADdPoQfTWTn5tcxp/E=
> Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate
> date: Thu, 29 May 2025 01:41:48 GMT
> server: uvicorn
> ```
> 
> Pretty vanilla--except for `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate`. Uvicorn lets you turn this off with `--ws-per-message-deflate false`, and with those arguments, no more disconnect! James is confirming that it fixes it for Shiny as well.

Fix: Disable permessage-deflate by default if RS_SERVER_URL is present

description:
Fixes https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/issues/1918

```python
# File: app-express.py

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A basic Shiny Chat example powered by Ollama.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

from chatlas import ChatOllama

from shiny.express import ui

# ChatOllama() requires an Ollama model server to be running locally.
# See the docs for more information on how to set up a local Ollama server.
# https://posit-dev.github.io/chatlas/reference/ChatOllama.html
chat_client = ChatOllama(model="llama3.2")

# Set some Shiny page options
ui.page_opts(
    title="Hello Ollama Chat",
    fillable=True,
    fillable_mobile=True,
)

# Create and display a Shiny chat component
chat = ui.Chat(
    id="chat",
    messages=["Hello! How can I help you today?"],
)
chat.ui()

### 
# New code
##
chat.enable_bookmarking(chat_client, store="url")
## / new code

# Generate a response when the user submits a message
@chat.on_user_submit
async def handle_user_input(user_input: str):
    response = await chat_client.stream_async(user_input)
    await chat.append_message_stream(response)
```

title: [WIP] fix(DataGrid): Allow columns with empty titles to be used in `DataGrid`
description:
Fixes: #1844 

The issue stems from the fact that TanStack uses column headers to create unique IDs, and an empty string is not a valid ID. Thus, my solution is to create a unique ID for the column with an empty header. Truth be told, there's no particular reason not to assign IDs equal to their corresponding headers for all the other columns, other that trying to change as little as possible.

Finding a unique ID is done through `findUnusedColumnName()` which was somewhat inspired by how {tibble} solves column name issues. In this case, the algorithm appends a space until it arrives at a string that doesn't exist in the list of column names. Again, the choice of space is arbitrary. What is important though is to keep in mind that this approach will fail if there is more than one column with an empty name. However, `DataGrid` currently doesn't work with duplicated names anyway, and generating unique IDs for all columns would probably be the solution.

Side note, I suspect that these large diffs in JS files are due to me using Windows, though I made sure that the output doesn't replace any LF with CRLF.

title: fix(input_select): Decouple `input_select()` and `input_selectize()`
description:
Fixes #1687

This PR follows the suggestions made in the issue and repurposes current `input_select()` implementation as `_input_select_impl()`. The new `input_select()` keeps the same signature but raises deprecation warnings upon using any of the three Selectize-related parameters.

Additionally, passing anything that's not a string (i.e. a HTML tag or `None`) as an option label raises another deprecation warning. The final goal would be to replace `_Choices = Mapping[str, TagChild]` with `_Choices = Mapping[str, str]`, but I guess that comes after a period of deprecation.

---

It's my first PR to this project, so if I missed some important part of the PR process, please let me know.

Here are a couple suggestions: * Tell me a joke * Tell me a story """ ui.br() chat = ui.Chat(id="chat") chat.ui( messages=[welcome], icon_assistant=faicons.icon_svg("otter"), ) ``` Currently, you get the default robot icon, when you should get an otter in the startup message. This isn't a problem for `append_message()` et al. since we're [already skipping the "tagify" step there for strings](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/blob/f2e774ca/shiny/ui/_chat_types.py#L32-L38). 2.
