title: fix(express): Find functions in the AST when a decorator renames them
description:
Fixes #2016.

## The bug

Express apps commonly generate several `@render.express` outputs in a loop, using a decorator to give each one a unique `__name__` (and therefore a unique output id):

```python
for label_name, label_ui in class_labels:
    with ui.value_box(showcase=ICONS[label_name]):
        @render.express
        @extend_name(f"_{label_name}")   # mutates fn.__name__
        def docs_label(): ...
```

This crashed with:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to find function 'docs_label_human_animal' in AST.
This should never happen, please file an issue!
```

## Root cause

`ast_matches_func()` located a function's `def` in its source AST by matching line number **and** `func.__name__`. But `__name__` is a mutable attribute that is merely *initialized* from the code object's name — any decorator can rewrite it. The AST node still says `docs_label` while `__name__` now says `docs_label_human_animal`, so nothing matched.

Notably, the two *downstream* stages of the same lookup (`match_name_and_lineno()` and `compare_decorated_code_objects()`) already keyed off `co_name`. Only the AST stage used `__name__` — a pre-existing inconsistency that the renaming decorator made observable.

## The fix

Match on `func.__code__.co_name`, which is fixed at compile time and always equals the name at the `def` site. One-line semantic change, plus a comment recording why it can't introduce a mis-match: the line number is the discriminating constraint and the name is only a secondary sanity check. A `def` line and a decorator line each belong to exactly one function, so `linenos` sets are disjoint across nodes.

## Diagnostics

The old message pointed users at a name that appeared nowhere in their source. Errors now report the code-object name (plus `__name__` when the two differ), name the file and line searched, and list likely causes:

```
Failed to find the definition of function 'real_source_name' (whose `__name__` has
since been changed to 'name_that_is_not_in_the_source') in the source of
'/path/app.py' (looking for a `def` at line 18).

This can happen if:
* The function is an `async def`. `expressify()` can only transform regular
  functions; use `@render.ui` instead of `@render.express`.
* A decorator between the `def` and `expressify()` replaced the function with a
  wrapper. Decorators applied below `expressify()` must return the original
  function, not a wrapper around it.
* The source file was modified after it was imported.

If none of these apply, please file an issue!
```

"This should never happen" is now reserved for the one lookup that genuinely shouldn't fail.

## Tests

30 new tests (11 → 41 across the two files). Rather than only checking that they pass, I reverted the helper to its pre-fix version and re-ran: **19 of the 30 fail against the old code**; the rest pin pre-existing behavior. All 11 original tests pass before and after, confirming no regression.

`tests/pytest/test_expressify_helpers.py` (new) — direct unit tests of `ast_matches_func()`, `find_code_for_func()`, `match_name_and_lineno()`: happy path, `co_firstlineno` pointing at either a decorator line or the `def` line, renames, same-name/different-line disambiguation, non-`FunctionDef` nodes.

`tests/pytest/test_display_decorator.py` — integration via `@expressify`, `expressify_unwrap_inplace()`, and `@render.express`. The ones that matter most for confidence:

- `test_rename_colliding_with_another_func_name` / `test_rename_does_not_match_the_colliding_def` — rename a function *onto the name of a different function in the same file* and assert we match the renamed function's own `def`, never the same-named decoy.
- `test_renamed_funcs_in_a_loop_keep_distinct_closures` — the issue's exact shape; each output renders its own value.
- `test_renamed_funcs_in_a_loop_share_one_cache_entry` — N renames of one `def` site produce exactly one `code_cache` entry. A cache bug here would make every value box show the same number, which is the user-visible symptom.
- `test_render_express_renamed_outputs_get_distinct_ids` — end-to-end: distinct `output_id`s, not one colliding id.

## Two known limitations, pinned rather than redesigned

Both are pre-existing design gaps in the parse-recompile-relocate mechanism, not things this fix should redesign. I pinned them in tests so any future change is deliberate:

- `test_expressify_async_is_unsupported` — `@expressify` cannot transform an `async def` (`ast_matches_func` only matches `ast.FunctionDef`). `@render.express` is unaffected; it rejects async up front with a clear `TypeError`. Probably deserves its own issue.
- `test_expressify_cannot_see_through_a_wrapper_below_it` — when a *wrapping* decorator sits between the `def` and `expressify()`, the function handed to expressify is the wrapper, so the inner body isn't captured. This is the one case where my change alters behavior: it was a misleading crash, now it's a silent no-op. `co_name` matching is correct here (it does identify the wrapper), but a silent no-op is worse to debug, so the new error text names wrapping decorators as a likely cause. I deliberately avoided a `__wrapped__`-based heuristic, which would catch `functools.wraps` decorators and miss hand-rolled ones — a half-guarantee that invites future confusion. Happy to revisit if you'd prefer a hard error.

## Verification

- 999 unit tests pass, 2 skipped.
- `uv run make format check-lint check-types` and `make check-pyright` clean (0 errors).
- Ran the issue's reproducer as a real Express app: renders two distinct outputs, `docs_label_a` and `docs_label_b`.

title: fix: Soft teardown of reactives when a session closes
description:
Ports rstudio/shiny#4421 to py-shiny. Same bug, same architecture, same fix.

## Problem

Since #2209 / #2264 (shipped in v1.6.1), closing a session tears down every reactive created in it: `AppSession._run_session_ended_tasks()` calls `destroy()` with the root namespace, which fires the weak destroy callback that each `reactive.Value` and `reactive.calc` registers at construction.

So any async continuation that outlives the websocket close errors on its first reactive access. Refreshing the page during in-flight async work is routine, which turns a previously benign race into a user-visible error. Reproduced in this checkout with a real `AppSession` and an `@reactive.extended_task` in flight when the connection drops:

```
errors: [DestroyedReactiveError("Reactive value 'None' has been destroyed.")]
status read raised: DestroyedReactiveError Reactive value 'None' has been destroyed.
```

The write comes from `ExtendedTask._done_callback` -> `_impl` (`shiny/reactive/_extended_task.py:199-215`), which sets `status`/`value`/`error` with no guard. It raises inside a bare `asyncio.create_task()`, so the exception is never retrieved, the queued invocations never run, `await flush()` is skipped, and the task is left in neither `"success"` nor `"error"`. User-created reactives fail identically.

The R report came in via shinychat, where the first reactive touched happened to be bslib's `Theme Counter`. py-shiny's `get_current_theme()` isn't backed by a session reactive, so that particular first-touch doesn't exist here — `ExtendedTask` is what bites, plus any user code holding a reactive across an `await` that outlives the close.

## Fix

A close is not a destroy, so the two are now distinguished:

- **On close**, reactive values and calcs are left intact, readable at their last value, and reclaimed by ordinary garbage collection. `on_destroy()` callbacks still fire, so module cleanup is unaffected, and effects are still destroyed via `Effect_`'s separate `on_ended(self.destroy)` registration.
- **On explicit `session.destroy(id)`** against a live session, teardown is unchanged and a later access still raises `DestroyedReactiveError` — there, a stale access is a genuine bug worth surfacing.

`_weak_callback()` becomes `_weak_destroy_callback(method, session)` and no-ops when that session is closed. No new state: `AppSession._is_closed()` reads `_has_run_session_ended_tasks`, which was already set at the top of `_run_session_ended_tasks()` before any teardown callback runs. `SessionProxy` delegates to its root (module-scoped reactives are exactly the ones that need the gate, and they hold a proxy, not an `AppSession`), and `ExpressStubSession` is never closed.

## Why not keep erroring on post-close access

- **Shiny's own code depends on it.** `ExtendedTask` sets its own status when its task settles, which routinely lands after a refresh. Under the old rule `ExtendedTask` itself was in violation.
- **App authors cannot comply.** The access is usually inside `ExtendedTask` or a library, not user code, and checking "is the session still up?" before the write is TOCTOU.
- **The write was already inert.** The session's effects are destroyed at `on_ended`, and outbound messages are dropped once the connection is closed (`shiny/_connection.py:71-73`). Verified by test: an effect does not re-run on a post-close write.
- **Erroring made teardown worse**, not better — the first error aborted the continuation and left `ExtendedTask` in a bogus state.

## Tests

12 new tests in `tests/pytest/test_destroy.py`. Verified by stashing only `shiny/reactive/_reactives.py`: **9 of the 12 fail** with the exact errors from the report.

- values and calcs readable *and* writable after close, and module reactives surviving a root close
- inputs readable after close
- an effect does **not** re-run on a post-close write (soft teardown must not resurrect the session)
- values are still garbage-collectable after close (soft teardown must not pin them)
- destroy callbacks still fire on close
- explicit module `destroy()` still raises `DestroyedReactiveError`; a `destroy()` that lands after close is a no-op rather than an error
- a real `ExtendedTask` that settles after close reaches `"success"` with its result, at both root and module scope, with an asyncio exception handler asserting no orphan-task errors

The bundled `shiny-for-python` Agent Skill (`references/session-lifecycle.md`) documents `on_ended`/`destroy`, so it gains the close-vs-destroy distinction in the same PR.

Full unit suite: `976 passed, 2 skipped`. `uv run make format check-lint check-types` and `make check-pyright` are clean.

## Follow-up, out of scope

Nothing cancels the underlying `asyncio` task at session end, so an in-flight extended task still runs to completion after disconnect rather than being torn down. R leaves its promise running too, so this PR matches upstream; cancelling on close would be a separate behavior change.

title: chore: Remove the httpx workaround for chatlas
description:
> [!WARNING]
> **Blocked — do not merge yet.** CI on this branch is expected to fail until the checklist below is complete. Kept as a draft so it cannot merge by accident.

Removes the `httpx` entry from the `dev` extra, added in #2437.

## Why it was there

chatlas imports `httpx` unconditionally but did not declare it, relying on `openai` to supply it transitively. `openai 3.0.0` (2026-08-12) switched to the separate `httpx2` distribution, so a fresh resolve installed no `httpx` at all and `import chatlas` raised `ModuleNotFoundError` — taking out the chatlas bookmark Playwright test on every Python version and browser.

`httpx` was declared directly as a stopgap. The real fix is upstream.

## Blocked on

- [ ] **posit-dev/chatlas#387 is resolved** — `fix: Declare the httpx dependency` (closes posit-dev/chatlas#386)
- [ ] **A chatlas release containing that fix is published to PyPI**
- [ ] **`chatlas>=<release>` floor raised in `pyproject.toml`** — see the note below

## Note on the third box

The first two boxes are the stated blockers. The third is one I added because removing `httpx` without also raising the chatlas floor would reintroduce the exact failure: `dev` currently pins only `chatlas>=0.6.1`, so a resolver is free to pick a pre-fix chatlas that still has the undeclared import. The floor needs to move to whatever release includes posit-dev/chatlas#387 — the version number is not known yet, which is why it is not in this diff.

## Verifying before merge

Once chatlas has released, confirm the removal is actually safe rather than assuming:

```bash
uv pip install -e ".[dev,test]"
python -c "import chatlas; print('ok')"
```

and check that `tests/playwright/shiny/bookmark/chat/chatlas/test_bookmark_chatlas.py` passes.

title: fix(tests): Add httpx to the dev extra for chatlas
description:
## Problem

`import chatlas` now raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx'`, which takes out `tests/playwright/shiny/bookmark/chat/chatlas/test_bookmark_chatlas.py` on every Python version and browser (13 failing jobs on an unrelated PR).

## Cause

Upstream drift, not a py-shiny change:

- `chatlas` does a bare `import httpx` in `_utils.py` and **does not declare httpx** in its dependencies — it relied on `openai` pulling it in transitively.
- **`openai 3.0.0`**, released **2026-08-12T01:55Z**, switched its HTTP dependency from `httpx` to the separate **`httpx2`** distribution (`httpx2<3,>=2.7.0`).

So a fresh resolve now installs `httpx2` and no `httpx`, and chatlas fails at import.

`main`'s last green run was 2026-08-11T16:58Z, before the openai release — this is not a regression from any merged PR, and `main` will hit it on its next run.

## Fix

Declare `httpx` directly in the `dev` extra, next to `chatlas`, until chatlas declares its own.

Verified in a clean environment that this is sufficient — `chatlas` works with `openai 3.0.0` as long as `httpx` is present alongside `httpx2`:

```
chatlas 0.21.0 | openai 3.0.0 | httpx 0.28.1 | httpx2 2.10.0
import chatlas OK
```

I chose adding `httpx` over pinning `openai<3` so we track openai forward rather than freezing it for an unrelated reason.

## Follow-up

Filing an issue upstream on chatlas for the undeclared dependency; the comment in `pyproject.toml` says to drop this line once that lands.

title: fix(build): Exclude nested api-examples and __pycache__ from the wheel
description:
Part of #2125.

## What

Two categories of extraneous files were shipping in the wheel.

**Nested `api-examples/`.** setuptools matches `exclude-package-data` patterns relative to each *package* directory, and `shiny` is the only package carrying data-file globs — so `api-examples/**` never reached `shiny/experimental/api-examples/`. One file leaked.

**`__pycache__`.** The `shiny = ["**"]` include glob matches it. Building a wheel from a working tree that had been imported produced **1303 files instead of 974** — 329 machine-specific `.pyc` files. CI builds from fresh checkouts, so released wheels were most likely unaffected, but that was luck rather than design.

## Tests

`tests/pytest/test_packaging.py` previously reimplemented setuptools' glob matching in Python and asserted against that model — which only proves the model agrees with itself, not that the wheel is clean. It now **builds a real wheel and reads its contents** (~3.4s, no network, built from a temp copy so it neither writes into the repo nor races under `pytest-xdist`).

It asserts that the bundled Agent Skills ship, that `api-examples` and bytecode do not, and that the total file count stays within bounds. The count bound has a **floor as well as a ceiling**: the ceiling guards against regressing #2125, the floor catches the opposite failure where a broken include glob silently drops an asset tree.

Each guard was mutation-tested rather than assumed to fire:

| mutation | caught by |
|---|---|
| drop `**/api-examples/**` | api-examples test — names the exact leaked file |
| drop `__pycache__` patterns | bytecode test **and** count test (1303 > 1100) |
| drop all exclusions | api-examples + bytecode tests |

The bytecode guard plants a sentinel `.pyc` into the copied tree so it fires deterministically, rather than depending on whether the working tree happens to have a `__pycache__`.

## Note on the issue

#2125 reports 1300+ files; a clean build off `main` was already at **975** (the top-level `api-examples` exclusion landed in #2304). This PR takes it to **974** and makes it deterministic.

The larger remaining item from the issue — moving `shiny/www/shared/sass/` (**308 files**) behind `shiny[theme]` — is **not** addressed here. Worth recording for whoever picks it up: 26 of the 28 presets ship only `.scss` sources with no precompiled CSS, so they are unusable without `libsass` and are dead weight for a plain `pip install shiny`. Only the `shiny` and `bootstrap` presets have a `bootstrap.min.css`, and those two are needed by every app at runtime.

Other remaining blocks, for reference: `datepicker/js` 87, `prism-code-editor/**` 61, `bootstrap/fonts` 39, `templates/**` 135.

## Caveat

The file-count bounds are a tripwire, not a spec. Anyone legitimately adding an asset tree will need to bump them; the failure message says so.

title: docs: use an absolute URL for the open-telemetry example link
description:
The `console` section of `shiny.otel`'s module docstring links to the example
with a repo-relative path:

```
See the [open-telemetry example](../../examples/open-telemetry/) for ...
```

That path only resolves in this repo's layout (`examples/open-telemetry/` is two
levels up from `shiny/otel/`). quartodoc renders this docstring into
py-shiny-site's `api/core/OpenTelemetry.html`, where the same relative path
resolves against the *site* layout and points at a page that does not exist —
py-shiny-site's new internal link checker flags it as a broken link.

Docstring links get rendered into the docs site, so they can't assume the repo's
directory layout. This switches it to the absolute GitHub tree URL, matching the
absolute markdown links already used elsewhere in the same docstring (e.g. the
"GitHub Issues" link). The other three references to the example
(`shiny/otel/__init__.py:166`, `:810`, and the otel skill reference doc) are
inline code rather than links, so they are unaffected.

Refs posit-dev/py-shiny-site#447

title: feat(session): Add `session.allow_reconnect()`
description:
Closes #2058.

Ports Shiny for R's `session$allowReconnect()` to Python:

```python
session.allow_reconnect(True)      # reconnect where the host supports it
session.allow_reconnect(False)     # default
session.allow_reconnect("force")   # always try; for local testing
```

The client-side support already existed in the vendored `shiny.js` — there's an `allowReconnect` message handler that sets `$allowReconnect` and, on disconnect, shows the countdown dialog and schedules `reconnect()`. Nothing was sending that message from Python, which is exactly what the issue reporter ran into (`Shiny.shinyapp.allowReconnect = false` with no way to change it).

### Implementation

`allow_reconnect()` is a **concrete** method on the `Session` ABC rather than an abstract one. It validates `True` / `False` / `"force"` and sends `{"allowReconnect": value}` via `_send_message_sync()`. Since `_send_message_sync()` is already specialized per subclass, `AppSession`, `SessionProxy` (delegates to the root session), and `ExpressStubSession` (no-op) all work with no per-class overrides, and a future `Session` subclass can't forget to implement it.

Validation uses identity checks (`value is not True and ...`) rather than `value not in (True, False, "force")`, because `1 == True` in Python — a membership test lets `0`, `1`, and `1.0` through, and the client then throws `Invalid value for allowReconnect: 1`.

Also adds the method to `docs/_quartodoc-core.yml` so it shows up in the API reference.

### Verification

Drove both example apps in a real browser:

- `$allowReconnect` arrives as `"force"` on the client.
- Closing the socket shows "Attempting to reconnect in 1s / Try now" instead of the "Disconnected from server" overlay.
- The client reconnects, and outputs keep updating afterward (counter went 1 → 2 across a reconnect).

### Notes

- Reconnecting requires the *host* to keep the session alive; `"force"` on a plain `shiny run` server starts a brand new session rather than resuming. This matches R's semantics and is documented.
- Unrelated upstream wart worth knowing: on the first flush after a reconnect, `OutputProgressReporter` in the vendored `shiny.js` logs `output ... is in an unexpected state of: 'value'` and drops that one value, so an output can briefly show a stale value until its next invalidation. Subsequent updates are fine. That's rstudio/shiny JS, not py-shiny, so it's left alone here.

### Supersedes #2102

#2102 (copilot-swe-agent) landed on the same API shape, and its docstring — derived from the R roxygen text at @schloerke's request — was better than my first draft, so I folded that wording in. Closing it in favor of this PR because:

- Its validation used `value not in (True, False, "force")`, which lets `1` / `0` through; its own `test_allow_reconnect_invalid_value` asserts `allow_reconnect(1)` raises and therefore fails.
- Its Core example is broken at runtime: `status = reactive.Value(...)` is shadowed by `@render.text def status()`, so the app renders `'text' object has no attribute 'get'`.
- No `_quartodoc-core.yml` entry, so the method wouldn't appear in the API reference.
- It's based on v1.5.0 and no longer applies: `@add_example("...")` is positional but `add_example()` has been keyword-only since #2329, and its new `## [UNRELEASED]` CHANGELOG heading conflicts with the existing `## [Unreleased]` section.

title: feat(theme): Support light and dark brand colors
description:
Companion to posit-dev/brand-yml#120.

## Summary

Extends `ui.Theme.from_brand()` to consume light/dark `brand.yml` colors and typography while preserving its existing scalar behavior.

- Applies light variants to ordinary documents without a `data-bs-theme` attribute and to explicit light mode.
- Emits complete mode-scoped Bootstrap and Shiny tokens, including RGB companions and derived component and utility styles, under the existing `data-bs-theme` selectors.
- Leaves compiled Bootstrap defaults intact when a mode-specific branch is undefined.
- Uses Bootstrap's configured Sass prefix rather than hard-coding `--bs-*`.
- Supports mode-specific link, heading, inline-code, and block-code colors and backgrounds.
- Temporarily installs `brand_yml` from the pinned upstream PR commit that provides the paired color model and CSS-variable API; restore a released version floor after publication.
- Updates the bundled Shiny theming skill with scalar, partial-variant, and runtime-switching guidance.

## Verification

```python
from brand_yml import Brand
from shiny import ui

brand = Brand.from_yaml_str(
    """
    color:
      primary: { light: "#0d6efd", dark: "#6ea8fe" }
      background: { light: "#ffffff", dark: "#212529" }
      foreground: { light: "#212529", dark: "#f8f9fa" }
    """
)
theme = ui.Theme.from_brand(brand)
page = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_dark_mode(),
    ui.input_action_button("action", "Action", class_="btn-primary"),
    theme=theme,
)
```

- [x] Complete unit suite passes: 1,063 passed and 1 skipped.
- [x] Nine Playwright cases pass across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit for default, explicit-light, dark, and runtime-switched styles.
- [x] Black, isort, Flake8, Pyright, and Pyrefly pass.
- [x] Bundled skill validation and `git diff --check` pass.

title: test(playwright): Log failed network requests when example apps hit console errors
description:
Refs #2431 (diagnostics only — does not fix the flake).

## Summary

The `console_errors` assertion in `tests/playwright/examples/example_apps.py` fails with `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)`, which does not say *which* resource 404'd. That is the main obstacle to diagnosing the webkit flake in #2431.

This adds two page listeners alongside the existing `console` one: `response` (collecting any status >= 400) and `requestfailed` (collecting network-level failures). The collected `METHOD url` entries are appended to the console-error assertion message, so the next occurrence names the resource. Favicon filtering — previously inline in the console handler — is factored into a shared `is_favicon()` helper so all three listeners skip it consistently. Console errors are now listed one per line instead of joined with a bare `"* "`.

No behavior change to what the test considers a failure: the assertion still triggers on console errors alone, and `failed_requests` is purely informational (the message says so explicitly when the list is empty, which itself is a useful signal — it would mean the 404 happened outside the page's request lifecycle).

## Verification

`pytest tests/playwright/examples/test_api_examples.py -k todo_list --browser chromium` passes, confirming the added listeners do not affect the passing path.

To see the new output, point `validate_example()` at an app whose UI references a missing asset (`ui.tags.script(src="/definitely-missing-asset.js")`). The assertion message becomes:

```
AssertionError: In app .../app-core.py had JavaScript console errors!
* Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
Failed network requests:
* HTTP 404 - GET http://127.0.0.1:21252/definitely-missing-asset.js
* net::ERR_ABORTED - GET http://127.0.0.1:21252/definitely-missing-asset.js
```

The duplicate entry is expected — Chromium reports both the 404 response and the subsequent aborted script load. Both are kept rather than deduped, since the pairing itself distinguishes a served-but-erroring response from a connection-level failure.

title: fix: Flush reactives by waking the session's message loop
description:
Fixes #1785. **Alternative to #2422** — same bug, different mechanism. See "Comparison with #2422" below.

## The issue

Reactivity work in Shiny only happens on a flush. `reactive.flush()` both recomputes and *delivers* (`AppSession._flush()` is itself registered as an `on_flushed` callback), and only the session's message loop was driving it. A download or dynamic-route handler runs on the ASGI request task, which is not a client message, so whatever it invalidated sat in the pending-flush queue, with the session stuck "busy" because the busy-count increments from the invalidated effects were never balanced, until an unrelated client message happened to arrive.

## The fix

The session's message loop now waits on a client message *or* an out-of-band flush request, whichever comes first. That is Shiny for R's split: `requestFlush()` only marks, and `serviceApp()` flushes on a later tick.

The consequence worth noting is *where* the flush ends up running. It happens on the session's own task, so it is ordered against client messages, it runs under the reactive lock the loop already takes, and a failure propagates into `_run_impl`'s existing error handling, which reports the error to the client and closes the session.

A flush is requested from two places:

1. [`_handle_request()`'s `finally`](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/pull/2449/files#diff-af4a1451ac386b2b3fe25b2e5eb15964b14f5c3ccaa34414b5c4920545839041R1356), for the `download` and `dynamic_route` actions. Those are the two that invoke app-author code; `upload` and `dataobj` only run Shiny's own plumbing, and uploads arrive one request per chunk, so asking there would be pure overhead. Streaming responses are skipped here, because their handler body has not run yet.
2. [Both content-wrapping generators' `finally`](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/pull/2449/files#diff-af4a1451ac386b2b3fe25b2e5eb15964b14f5c3ccaa34414b5c4920545839041R1484), for streaming downloads, whose handler body runs only when Starlette iterates the response. `finally` and not a trailing statement, because a handler can raise part-way through and a client can cancel mid-stream, and neither path may skip the flush.

### The risky part

[`_run_impl`'s receive](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/pull/2449/files#diff-af4a1451ac386b2b3fe25b2e5eb15964b14f5c3ccaa34414b5c4920545839041R1065) stops being a bare `await` and becomes a task, so the loop can wait on either it or a flush request. When a flush wins the race the in-flight receive is *carried over* to the next iteration rather than recreated. Recreating it would drop a client message, which is considerably worse than the bug being fixed, so two tests pin it: one for the parked case and one for twenty messages interleaved with twenty flush requests, asserting each is processed exactly once and in order.

### Why this is not wired to `_request_flush()`

The obvious move is to implement the existing `AppSession._request_flush()` stub, whose TODO points at exactly this. That turns out to be a trap, and the first version of this PR fell into it.

`send_input_message()` calls `_request_flush()`, and that is how every `ui.update_*()` delivers itself: it registers a `session.on_flush` callback that calls `send_input_message()`, and session flush callbacks run *inside* a flush. So queueing a message would re-arm the loop from within the flush it was already part of. That costs an extra empty flush per interaction — broadcast to every connected session, since the flush is global — and with an `on_flush(..., once=False)` callback that queues a message it never settles: measured **999 flushes with zero client input**, where `main` is idle after one.

So the out-of-band request is a separate `_request_out_of_band_flush()`, and `_request_flush()` is left as the stub it has always been. Making it live up to its name needs a way to distinguish "deliver the outbound queue" from "flush the reactive graph", which is a bigger change than this bug warrants. `send_input_message()` from outside the message cycle therefore still waits for the next client message, exactly as on `main`.

### A separate bug this uncovered

[`shiny_otel_span_stream()`](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/pull/2449/files#diff-62a8e9ac8bdf0cfbe37a8cfc23ce365b227bbe922d023370f8a9524d1937297f) did `async for chunk in inner: yield chunk` without ever closing `inner`, so a consumer that stops early — Starlette closing the body iterator when a client cancels a download — abandoned the wrapped generator mid-yield and left its cleanup to the garbage collector.

That makes the download handler's `finally` arbitrarily late. CI caught it on Python 3.10, where the abort test failed while passing on 3.12 and 3.14, with the wrapped generator's `session_context` exit surfacing as a pytest unraisable exception, which is the signature of GC finalization rather than close. Reproduced locally with `uv run --python 3.10` and fixed by closing `inner` in a `finally`, with a direct test in `test_otel_download.py`.

This is not specific to the approach here: any cleanup in the content-wrapping generators has the same problem, so **#2422 is affected identically** and needs the same fix.

## Comparison with #2422

#2422 fixes the same issue by scheduling a fire-and-forget `asyncio.create_task` that takes the reactive lock and flushes, from the same two hook points. Both fix #1785, both cover `dynamic_route`, and both leave `send_input_message()` alone. Differences that bear on the choice:

- **Error handling.** There, nothing awaits the task, so a failing flush can only be logged with `traceback.print_exc()`. Here it flows through `_run_impl`'s handler and is reported to the client.
- **Lock contention.** There, the download's task takes the reactive lock, which is the first code in py-shiny to contend it; that bound the process-global `asyncio.Lock` to a since-closed event loop and broke `test_poll` in the same xdist worker, needing a separate fix to `ReactiveEnvironment.lock`. No request task takes the lock here, so that latent bug is not tripped. It is still a real latent bug and worth fixing on its own merits.
- **OTel.** There, the spawned task inherits the download span's context, so the flush needs `detached_otel_context()` or the whole `reactive_update` subtree nests under `download` and inflates its duration. Not an issue here.
- **Blast radius.** This one edits the message loop, the hot path for every session. That is the argument for #2422: it is contained. The mitigation here is coverage rather than assertion — see Verification.
- **Ordering.** Here the flush is serialised with client messages by construction. There it races them.
- **Not fixed by either.** The handler's own `set()` calls still run outside the reactive lock, so a concurrent client-driven flush can still publish a mid-stream value early. Locking the handler would mean holding the lock for a whole streaming download and blocking every session.

## Tests

[`tests/pytest/test_out_of_band_flush.py`](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/pull/2449/files#diff-9fa12df955dcd9d398b429f858a15972a28e4f518cce167734a228a88edcc44c) drives a real `AppSession` over a `MockConnection`, waits for it to park waiting for a client message the way it does when a browser asks for a download, then issues the request through the real ASGI path. Eleven tests: the three handler forms, flush-after-stream-end, handler raises mid-stream, client aborts mid-stream, repeated downloads, `dynamic_route`, the spin guard, and the two message-loop regression guards.

One note on `_read_body()`, which yields to the event loop generously between chunks. A real ASGI server awaits `send()` per chunk, and without that the session's task never runs mid-stream, so a test cannot tell "flushed once at the end" from "flushed during the stream" — the stream-end test passed against a broken implementation until this was fixed.

## Verification

`uv run make format check-lint check-types` and `make check-pyright` clean. Unit suite 1078 passed on Python 3.12 and on 3.10, single-process and under xdist. Because this touches the message loop: the full `tests/playwright/shiny` suite (339 passed), `tests/playwright/examples` (360 passed; two failures are this machine missing `pytz` and an un-built `shinymediapipe`), and an adversarial script covering interleaved messages and flush requests, a flush requested from inside message handling, and cancellation with a receive in flight — under `asyncio` debug mode with warnings as errors.

A code review pass found four issues, all fixed and each verified before and after: the `send_input_message` spin above, the premature flush for streaming responses, the stream-end test that asserted a property of its own harness, and an unretrieved exception on a receive task the loop never consumed. CI then found the Python 3.10 generator-finalization bug, which is why the unit suite is now run on both versions locally.

title: fix(playwright): keep remote browser server open with tty
description:
## Summary

Mitigates intermittent remote Playwright browser connection drops and adds container state diagnostics to CI workflows on failure.

## Changes

- **Mitigate remote server stdin exit**: Add `--tty` to `docker run` in `.github/py-shiny/setup-playwright-remote/action.yaml` so the detached container allocates a pseudo-TTY and keeps stdin open.
- **Safe page reset**: In `tests/playwright/conftest.py`, catch and swallow exceptions when closing a broken or crashed page during test reset so secondary cleanup errors do not mask the root cause.
- **Failure diagnostics**: Add failure steps in `.github/workflows/pytest.yaml`, `.github/workflows/deploy-tests.yaml`, and `.github/py-shiny/setup-playwright-remote/action.yaml` to dump container state (`docker inspect --format '{{json .State}}'`) and container logs (`docker logs`) to clearly identify `OOMKilled`, crash exits, or clean exits.
- **Tests**: Add unit test coverage in `tests/pytest/test_playwright_reliability.py` for safe page reset error handling and verify the `--tty` flag.

title: docs: clarify how to install shiny's bundled Agent Skills
description:
## Problem

The README and `shiny skills --help` both handed users this:

```sh
uvx library-skills --claude
```

Two things go wrong with that as written:

1. **It doesn't name shiny.** You're reading shiny's README, and you get a command with no "shiny" in it. There's nothing in the command to tell you what it installs.
2. **The precondition is implicit.** `library-skills` reads the *current project's* dependencies and installs the skills bundled with the packages you have installed. Run it in a fresh directory — or in a clone of this repo — and it finds nothing, with no hint as to why. The old text said "once `shiny` is a dependency of your project" but never said "run this from that project."

## What changed

Prose only — no behavior change, no new commands.

- `README.md` — lead with why an agent wants these docs, state the "run this from your project directory" precondition explicitly, explain what `library-skills` actually does (reads your deps, symlinks so skills track your installed version), and mention `shiny skills list` for looking without installing.
- `shiny/_main/_skills.py` — same reframing in the `skills` group help and the `skills list` footer.
- `.claude/references/agent-skills.md` — note for contributors that `library-skills` is run from the *user's* project, not a clone of this repo.

## Considered and rejected

Adding a `shiny skills install` subcommand. It would name shiny and need no bootstrap, but it reinvents `library-skills` — which is maintained by tiangolo, used by FastAPI to ship its own skills, and already handles Windows symlink fallback, drift detection, and per-agent target directories. Not shiny's wheel to rebuild.

## Verification

- `uv run make format check-lint check-types` — clean
- `tests/pytest/test_packaging.py` — 8 passed
- `shiny skills --help` and `shiny skills list` render correctly (checked manually)

A matching py-shiny-site PR updates `get-started/agent-skills.qmd`.

title: test(playwright): Make pytest-playwright's --tracing flag work
description:
## What was broken

`tests/playwright/conftest.py` overrides pytest-playwright's `page` fixture with a session-shared page built from `browser.new_page()`. `browser` is a `Browser`, not a `BrowserContext`, so `new_page()` creates an implicit context with default options. pytest-playwright records `--tracing`, `--video`, and `--screenshot` artifacts only in its own function-scoped `context` fixture, which this suite never instantiates. The flags parsed successfully and silently wrote nothing, which is easy to mistake for "the run produced no failures worth tracing".

## The change

A session-scoped `_session_context` fixture now creates the context via `browser.new_context(**browser_context_args)` and owns the shared page, and it calls `context.tracing.start(...)` when `--tracing` is on or retain-on-failure.

Tracing normally starts and stops per test, but the whole point of this suite's `page` fixture is that the page (and therefore its context) outlives every individual test. `tracing.start_chunk()` / `stop_chunk()` is the mechanism for that case: an autouse function-scoped `_trace_chunk` fixture opens a chunk per test and writes it out, slicing one long-lived trace into a file per test without giving up the shared page. A `pytest_runtest_makereport` hookwrapper records the outcome on the item so retain-on-failure can tell a pass from a failure.

Traces are written to `<output>/<slug>/trace.zip` rather than a flat `<slug>.trace.zip`. That matches pytest-playwright's own artifact layout and the `test-results/*/trace.zip` location `make playwright-show-trace` already looked in; a flat layout would not.

## Using it

```bash
# One trace per test, written to test-results/<test>/trace.zip
make playwright-shiny SUB_FILE="inputs/test_foo.py" PYTEST_EXTRA_ARGS="--tracing on"

# Open the newest trace, or a specific one with TRACE="path/to/trace.zip"
make playwright-show-trace
```

`PYTEST_EXTRA_ARGS` is new: the `playwright` targets had no way to pass a one-off pytest option. Use `--tracing retain-on-failure` to keep traces only for failures. Tracing does not need `--headed`, so the default headless runs record fine: a trace's screenshots and DOM snapshots come from the renderer, which headless still rasterizes.

`make playwright-show-trace` also changes. It passed the whole `test-results/*/trace.zip` glob to `playwright show-trace`, which accepts exactly one trace and exits with "too many arguments" given more. That never came up while the flag recorded nothing, but one trace per test makes it the normal case, so the target now opens the newest trace and takes `TRACE=` to pick another.

Both commands are documented in CLAUDE.md's testing shortcuts and in the testing section of `.claude/references/architecture.md`.

## Caveats

`--video` now records, but as one continuous video for the whole session rather than one per test. Video is a context-level option and there is no video equivalent of `start_chunk()`, so per-test video would mean giving up the shared page, which is what makes this suite fast. `--screenshot` remains a no-op: the plugin captures screenshots when tearing down its own `page` fixture, which this conftest replaces. Both are documented in the NOTE in `tests/playwright/playwright-pytest.ini`, replacing the now-stale claim that all three options do nothing.

No CHANGELOG entry: this is developer-facing test infrastructure, matching how recent commits in this area were handled (#2432, #2306, #2295).

## Verification

`uv run make format check-lint check-types` is clean, and so is `uv run make check-pyright`. Both are needed here: `check-types` runs only pyrefly, while CI runs pyright as its own job, and pyright's strict mode rejected the first version of these fixtures (`FixtureRequest.node` is unannotated in pytest, `getoption("--output")` is `Any | None`, and a `hookwrapper=True` generator is sent pluggy's `Result`, not `None`).

`--tracing on` over `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/` (42 tests) produced exactly 42 `trace.zip` files, one per test, each containing `trace.trace`, `trace.network`, and screenshot resources. Rerunning under `-n 4` produced the same 42 with no filename collisions, and a serial (`-n 0`) run behaves the same. `--tracing retain-on-failure` over a scratch pass/fail pair wrote a trace only for the failing test. With the default `--output`, the resulting paths match the `test-results/*/trace.zip` glob (checked directly rather than by launching the interactive viewer).

Through the make targets: `make playwright-shiny ... PYTEST_EXTRA_ARGS="--tracing on"` wrote one trace per test under `test-results/`, and `make playwright-show-trace` resolved to exactly one trace both by default (newest) and via `TRACE=`.

The default path is unregressed: `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/` plus `tests/playwright/shiny/bugs/` (62 tests) passed on chromium with no tracing flags and wrote no artifacts.

title: fix: show_offcanvas() accepts a string id and tag content
description:
Fixes #2445

## Summary

`ui.show_offcanvas()` now dispatches on the type of its first argument, matching bslib's `show_offcanvas()` (rstudio/bslib#1346):

- a string `id` of an `offcanvas()` panel already in the UI → reveals it (same as `toggle_offcanvas(id, show=True)`)
- tag content (e.g. `ui.p(...)`, `htmltools.HTML(...)`, `ui.markdown(...)`) → wrapped into a new anonymous panel
- an `Offcanvas` object → rendered + shown (unchanged)

Previously, `show_offcanvas()` only accepted an `Offcanvas` object; passing a string id raised an unhandled `AttributeError` deep inside the implementation (#2445). A string that looks like body text instead of an id (empty, or containing whitespace) now raises an actionable `ValueError` instead of being silently misinterpreted.

## Examples

Revealing an existing panel by id:

```python
from shiny import App, Inputs, Outputs, Session, reactive, ui

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.offcanvas(ui.p("Body."), title="Settings", id="settings"),
    ui.input_action_button("show", "Show settings"),
)

def server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):
    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.show)
    def _():
        ui.show_offcanvas("settings")

app = App(app_ui, server=server)
```

Showing server-rendered Markdown content in a new anonymous panel:

```python
from shiny import App, Inputs, Outputs, Session, reactive, ui

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_action_button("show_notes", "Show release notes"),
)

def server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):
    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.show_notes)
    def _():
        ui.show_offcanvas(
            ui.markdown(
                """
                ## Release notes

                - Added **markdown** support in server-rendered panels.
                - See the [docs](https://shiny.posit.co) for details.
                """
            )
        )

app = App(app_ui, server=server)
```

## Implementation notes

- Related bslib PR: rstudio/bslib#1346. bslib assets are already up to date in py-shiny (#2446), so this is a pure Python port with no client-side changes.
- The string-id path delegates to the existing `toggle_offcanvas(id, show=True, session=session)` rather than duplicating the send logic.
- `hide_offcanvas()` / `toggle_offcanvas()` are unchanged; `toggle_offcanvas` accepting an `Offcanvas` object too (for full parity with `hide_offcanvas`) was raised in #2445 as a separate, independent question and is out of scope here.

title: feat(cli): Add developer CLI tools (validate, simulate, inspect with Reactlog, docs, scaffold)
description:
### Summary of Changes

Adds first-class developer CLI subcommands directly into `shiny` for terminal users, CI/CD pipelines, and local development workflows.

#### 🛠️ Developer CLI Subcommands

- **`shiny docs [COMPONENT]`**: Runtime component reflection for signatures, category filtering, docstrings, and copyable snippets.
- **`shiny scaffold [TEMPLATE]`**: Instant starter templates (`express_dashboard`, `core_dashboard`, `ai_chat`) emitted to stdout or written to file.

#### ⏱️ Reactlog-Style Reactive Tracing
- Traces chronological reactive events: `define`, `valueChange`, `invalidate`, `flushStart`, `calculate`, `dependsOn`, and `ready`.
- Exports an interactive time-scrubber web visualizer via `shiny inspect app.py --html reactlog.html`.

#### 🧪 Testing & Verification

- Formatted and linted with Black, isort, and Flake8.

title: fix(input_slider): Encode date and naive datetime values as UTC
description:
Fixes #2398.

Two instances of the same defect in `_as_numeric()` (`shiny/ui/_input_slider.py`), which encodes slider values as epoch milliseconds for the client. `input_slider()` and `update_slider()` share it, so both were affected.

## 1. `date` values lost a day (the reported bug)

Dates were encoded as **local** midnight:

```python
return datetime(x.year, x.month, x.day).timestamp() * 1000
```

but the client formats and reads slider dates back in **UTC** — `strftime.utc()` for the displayed label, `formatDateUTC(new Date(Number(val)))` in `SliderInputBinding.getValue()`. For any positive UTC offset, local midnight is the previous calendar day in UTC, so a day is lost on the round trip. Negative-offset timezones are unaffected, which is likely why this went unnoticed.

It reads as an update-only bug because the initial `min`/`max`/`value` are all shifted consistently — the slider looks internally coherent until you compare a `date` you passed in against the `date` you get back.

**Fix:** encode UTC midnight. This also matches Shiny for R, where `as.numeric(<Date>) * 86400000` is UTC midnight by construction.

## 2. Naive `datetime` values shifted by the server's offset

Same asymmetry: `.timestamp()` interprets a **naive** datetime as local time, but the `shiny.datetime` input handler decodes the value the client returns as UTC.

```
UTC                naive 2025-01-01 12:00 -> 2025-01-01 12:00   aware -> 2025-01-01 12:00
Europe/Amsterdam   naive 2025-01-01 12:00 -> 2025-01-01 11:00   aware -> 2025-01-01 12:00
Pacific/Kiritimati naive 2025-01-01 12:00 -> 2024-12-31 22:00   aware -> 2025-01-01 12:00
America/New_York   naive 2025-01-01 12:00 -> 2025-01-01 17:00   aware -> 2025-01-01 12:00
```

**Fix:** anchor naive datetimes to UTC so they round-trip unchanged. Timezone-aware datetimes name an absolute instant and are untouched — they already round-tripped correctly.

This one is a deliberate behavior change rather than a pure bug fix: the *instant* was preserved before, only its wall-clock representation moved, and R has no naive `POSIXct` to compare against. But "what you pass in is what you get back" is the only defensible reading of a value that carries no offset.

## Scope

These are the only two places py-shiny converts a date/datetime to an epoch number for the client. `input_date`, `input_date_range`, `update_date`, and `update_date_range` all go through `_as_date_attr()`, which emits `"%Y-%m-%d"` strings and is timezone-safe.

## Tests

**Unit** — new `tests/pytest/test_input_slider.py`, parametrized over 8 timezones from `Etc/GMT+12` to `Pacific/Kiritimati` (including the fractional `Asia/Kathmandu` +05:45 and `Pacific/Chatham` +12:45/+13:45) via `time.tzset()`, skipped where `tzset` is unavailable. Covers `date`, naive `datetime`, and aware `datetime`. Every non-UTC zone fails against the pre-fix code.

**End-to-end** — new `tests/playwright/shiny/inputs/input_slider_timezone/`. The app sets `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` (+14:00) *before* building the UI, so the round trip is exercised against a forward-offset server no matter which timezone CI runs in. It checks initial values, values after `update_slider()`, and values chosen by dragging in the browser, for both a `date` and a naive `datetime` slider. Reverting either branch of `_as_numeric()` independently fails it (`2024-05-31` and `2024-05-31 10:00:00` respectively).

**Also fixed:** `convert_to_utc_date()` in the existing slider Playwright test mirrored the same local-midnight conversion as the buggy code, so it masked the bug and contradicted its own name. It now uses UTC, like its `convert_to_utc_date_time()` sibling.

## Verification

```
uv run make format check-lint check-types   # clean
uv run make check-pyright                   # 0 errors
pytest tests/pytest                         # 1076 passed, 2 skipped
```

Both slider Playwright suites pass under `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=America/New_York` (9 tests each).

title: ci: Upgrade astral-sh/setup-uv to v10.0.1 for manifest fetch retries
description:
Fixes #2459.

`astral-sh/setup-uv@v8.2.0` resolves the uv version by fetching a manifest from `raw.githubusercontent.com`, and in that release the request has a 5 second timeout and no retry. One transient connection error kills the job during setup, which is what happened in [this "Run deploy tests" job](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/32180773599/job/95853003964). Upstream added three retries with backoff around that fetch in [astral-sh/setup-uv#1016](https://github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/pull/1016), first released in v10.0.1.

All three call sites move to v10.0.1, including the narwhals integration job that was still on the floating `v7` tag and has the same exposure. The two guard messages in the narwhals composite actions referenced `@v7`, so they are updated to match.

## Notes for review

Pinning an exact uv `version:` instead would not have avoided this. The download path calls `getArtifact()`, which fetches the same manifest, and the runner tool cache misses on a fresh image.

The upgrade crosses two major versions, and only one breaking change affects us. v9.0.0 flipped the `prune-cache` default from `true` to `false`, so this PR sets `prune-cache: true` explicitly to keep cache behavior identical to today rather than letting it drift as a side effect of a reliability fix. The reasoning is in a comment next to the input. v10.0.0's breaking change only applies to `enable-cache: auto`, and we set `enable-cache: true`.

Verified that the retry is present in the shipped `dist/setup/index.cjs` bundle at the v10.0.1 tag, not only in source, and that every input we pass is still declared in that release's `action.yml`.

This only takes effect for CI runs after merge, so the fix cannot be demonstrated in this PR's own checks.

title: refactor(data frame): Address columns by position on the Python side
description: Follow-up from reviewing #2421. Stacked on #2456, but independent of it — this one is Python-only and could be rebased onto `main` if you'd rather land it separately. Two internal paths translated a column index into a column *name* and then back again. Column names are not dependable identifiers — they may be empty, and pandas allows names that are not strings — so both now stay positional. ## 1. `apply_frame_patches()` — fewer hops It grouped patches into a `dict` keyed by column name, looked each name up with `nw_data.columns[index]`, and read the column back with `get_column(name)`. Patches arrive from the browser keyed by column index, so the dict is now keyed by index and the column is read positionally with `nw_data[:, index]`. That drops both name lookups, and with them the `dict[Any, ScatterValues]` key type (and its explanatory comment) that the non-string-name case had forced. One implicit name step remains and is unavoidable: `with_columns()` matches the scattered Series back onto the frame by its name. That's noted in a comment rather than hidden. ## 2. `subset_frame(cols=)` — narrower internals, same caller-facing input Callers may still pass names or positions, but resolution now happens once, in a new `as_col_indexes()`, and everything downstream is typed `ColIndexes` (positions only). Things that were previously implicit are now documented, validated, and tested: - An integer is **always** a position, never a pandas integer label. The two can't be told apart, and narwhals reads a list of ints in the column slot positionally, so a frame labelled `{5: ..., 3: ...}` has to be addressed by position. - "Integer" means anything integer-like, not just `int`. `isinstance(np.int64(5), int)` is `False`, so a numpy integer used to take the *name* branch and resolve by label equality — inverting the rule for exactly the values `np.where()` and `Index.get_indexer()` produce. Detection is `__index__`-based, and `ColsList` is widened from `str | int` to `str | SupportsIndex` to match. - `bool` is a `TypeError`. It is a subclass of `int`, so `[True, False]` would otherwise read as positions `[1, 0]`. `StyleInfo`'s `cols` accepts a bool mask; this deliberately does not, rather than silently accepting a third form. - Positions are bounds-checked. A negative position used to select from the end of the frame, and an out-of-range one escaped as narwhals' `IndexError: positional indexers are out-of-bounds`; both now raise a `ValueError` naming the position, as `update_cell_value()` and `style_info_cols()` already do. - An unknown name raises `ValueError: Column name 'nope' not found in the data frame. To select a column by position, pass an int.` instead of `ValueError: 'nope' is not in list`. ## Also recorded, not fixed While testing this I found that on **polars**, any selection that names columns positionally renames a column named `""` to `"column_"` — for `["a", "", "c"]`, `data[:, [0, 1, 2]]` gives `["a", "column_1", "c"]` and `data[:, [2, 1]]` gives `["c", "column_1"]`. It applies to the rows-and-columns branch too; only the rows-only branch is unaffected. No caller in shiny selects columns by position — `data_view()` passes `rows=` only — so this is latent. It's documented in the `subset_frame` docstring rather than worked around, since working around it would mean selecting by name and reintroducing the dependence on names this PR removes. Happy to file it upstream if you think it's a narwhals bug. No user-facing behavior change, so no CHANGELOG entry. ## Verification Rebased onto the updated #2421 head (`011c63b2`) — this commit applied cleanly, since the new work on #2421 is all client-side. - New tests: `apply_frame_patches` on an empty-named column (pandas **and** polars), and `as_col_indexes` covering name resolution, int pass-through, mixed input, the empty list, the unknown-name error, the int-is-a-position rule (pinned with an int that is *also* a label, the only input where the two readings differ), numpy integers, negative and out-of-range positions, and `bool`. - `tests/pytest` — 1111 passed, 2 skipped. - `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame` + `.../bugs/1844-datagrid-empty-column-name` — 48 passed, 1 rerun (the known `test_single_selection` flake). - `uv run make format check-lint check-types` and `make check-pyright` — clean, 0 errors. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: refactor(data frame): Rename the client's `columns` state to `columnNames`
description: Follow-up from reviewing #2421. Cosmetic; stacked on #2455. Inside the data frame client, `columns` held column *names* while `cols`, `colIndex`, and the sort/filter payloads all hold column *indices*, so the two kinds of column identifier were hard to tell apart at a glance — which is how #1844 was able to hide: a name was being used where an id was needed. ## Scope This is a rename of local identifiers only: - `columns` state → `columnNames` (and `setColumns` → `setColumnNames`, `columnsProp` → `columnNamesProp`) - the incoming `newColumns` in `updateData()` → `newColumnNames` - the `colname` loop variable → `columnName` **The wire contract is unchanged.** The `columns` key of the payload and of the `updateData` message is `FrameJson["columns"]` on the Python side, so renaming it would be a coordinated protocol change rather than a cosmetic one. `updateData()` destructures it as `columns: newColumnNames` at the boundary, with a comment saying so. If you'd rather rename the wire field too (and `PandasData.columns` with it), say the word and I'll extend this PR. The type widening I'd noted on #2421 has since landed there as `ColumnNames = ReadonlyArray`, so this PR is purely the naming half. No behavior change. ## Verification Rebased onto the updated #2421 head (`011c63b2`) and re-verified there. The rename was re-applied by hand rather than patch-merged, since #2421 rewrote `updateData()` in the meantime. - `make js-build` (`tsc --noEmit` + eslint + esbuild) — clean; `shiny/www` bundle rebuilt in this commit. Only the source map changes: the minified `data-frame.js` is byte-identical, since the rename touches local identifiers only. - `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame` + `tests/playwright/shiny/bugs/1844-datagrid-empty-column-name` — 48 passed. - `tests/pytest` — 1104 passed, 1 skipped. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: refactor(data frame): Drop the unused `columns` prop from the cell edit path
description: Follow-up from reviewing #2421. Stacked on it because it touches the same lines. `TableBodyCell` took a `columns` prop and forwarded it to `updateCellsData()`, but neither read it: the cell edit path identifies its target entirely by `rowIndex`/`columnIndex`, and the patch payload sent to the server is `{row_index, column_index, value}`. The prop was also a dependency of the save `useCallback`, so the callback was recreated whenever the columns array identity changed. Also drops dependencies the surrounding effects do not read: `columns` from the `addPatches` and `updateData` listener effects, `setSorting` from the `addPatches` effect, and `resetCellEditMap` and `setTableData` from the `updateData` effect, whose body only calls `updateData(evtData)` and so reaches them through that callback's own closure. **This does not make anything re-run less often**, and an earlier version of this description claimed otherwise — thanks @jat255 for catching it. `useCellEditMap()` returns a fresh `setCellEditMapAtLoc` and `resetCellEditMap` on every render, so those deps already invalidate on every render, which is a superset of every columns change. Making the re-runs less frequent means stabilizing those identities inside `useCellEditMap()` — a separate change, happy to do it as a follow-up. This PR stands on the deps being dead, not on a re-render win. ## Why this is worth doing #2421 establishes that column *names* are not usable identifiers — they can be empty, and pandas allows names that are not strings. Auditing the client for other sites that carry names turned up exactly two, and both were dead. With them gone, the client reads a column name in exactly two places, both deliberate: the header label (`header: String(columnName)`) and the sort/filter migration in `updateData()` that #2421 added, which has to match by name to follow a column across a reorder. Dropping the prop makes the `ColumnNames` import unused in both `cell.tsx` and `data-update.tsx`, so it goes too. No behavior change. ## Verification Rebased onto the updated #2421 head (`011c63b2`) and re-verified there. - `make js-build` (runs `tsc --noEmit` + eslint + esbuild) — clean, and the checked-in `shiny/www` bundle is rebuilt in this commit. Confirmed again after the rebase that a clean rebuild of the parent branch reproduces its committed bundle byte-for-byte, so the bundle diff here is only this change. - `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame` + `tests/playwright/shiny/bugs/1844-datagrid-empty-column-name` — 48 passed. - `tests/pytest` — 1104 passed, 1 skipped. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

Your project ranks in the upper [rating bands](https://inspect.software/wiki/scoring-bands) of our open-source health index (which measures maintainability, responsiveness, and security). - **Transparent:** Links directly to [your full report](https://inspect.software/software/posit-dev/py-shiny), based on our open [methodology](https://inspect.software/methodology).

If you prefer to keep your README minimal, feel free to close this PR without replying. [Your report](https://inspect.software/software/posit-dev/py-shiny) will remain publicly available and up-to-date either way.

title: fix(playwright): Allocate remote server ports dynamically
description:
## Summary

- The action selects an available container port when `port` is empty.
- Docker selects an available host port and returns it to the action.
- The readiness probe and pytest use the resolved host port.
- A caller can still set `port` for a fixed mapping.

## Problem

The action used port `43424` for every remote Playwright server. A port collision stopped `run-server` before the tests started.

Closes #2444

title: feat(cli): Add shiny inspect command with Reactlog visualization and interactive HTML export
description:
### Overview

Adds `shiny inspect` subcommand to `shiny` CLI for statically inspecting and visualizing reactive dependency graphs (DAG) with simulated invalidation ordering and interactive HTML export.

| Feature | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Terminal DAG View** | Displays reactive nodes (inputs, calcs, effects, outputs) and dependency edges in the terminal |
| **Reactlog Simulation** | Simulates step-by-step invalidation lifecycle events (`define`, `assumeValue`, `propagate`, `wouldEvaluate`, `dependsOn`, `ordered`) |
| **Interactive HTML Export** | Generates standalone HTML visualizer with Sugiyama layered layout, timeline scrubber, source code view, and hover dependency highlighting |
| **Graph Formats** | Supports Mermaid (`--mermaid`), Graphviz DOT (`--dot`), and JSON (`--json`) output |

---

### Command Examples

```bash
# Terminal trace & dependency map
$ shiny inspect app.py
$ shiny inspect app.py --reactlog

# Interactive visualizer HTML export
$ shiny inspect app.py --html reactlog.html

# Mermaid / JSON / DOT exports
$ shiny inspect app.py --mermaid
$ shiny inspect app.py --json
$ shiny inspect app.py --dot
```

title: feat(cli): Add shiny docs command for component and controller documentation lookup with autocomplete
description:
### Overview

Adds a dedicated `shiny docs` CLI command to inspect signatures, types, parameters, and docstrings directly from the terminal for functions, classes, Playwright controllers, and nested methods.

---

### Key Capabilities

1. **AST Signature Extraction (Line 1)**: Signatures are read directly from the source AST rather than reconstructed runtime signatures, presenting type annotations and defaults on the first line, followed by the docstrings.
2. **Multi-Component Lookups in One Call**: Supports multiple arguments in a single command invocation, separated by `---` blocks for readability.
3. **Controller & Method Lookups**: Supports inspecting Playwright controllers and their individual methods (e.g. `shiny.playwright.controller.Accordion.expect_height`, `Accordion.expect_height`, `controller.Accordion.expect_height`).
4. **Shell Tab Completion & Programmatic Autocomplete**:
   - Native Click shell completion (`shell_complete`) for interactive bash/zsh/fish tab completion.
   - Programmatic `--complete <PREFIX>` option for agent and script query completion.
5. **JSON Mode**: `--json` flag for structured machine consumption of docs and completion items.

---

### Command Examples

#### 1. Single Component Lookup
```bash
$ shiny docs shiny.ui.value_box
```
```text
def value_box(title: TagChild, value: TagChild, *args: TagChild | TagAttrs, showcase: Optional[TagChild]=None, showcase_layout: SHOWCASE_LAYOUTS_STR | ShowcaseLayout='left center', full_screen: bool=False, theme: Optional[str | ValueBoxTheme]=None, height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, max_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, min_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, fill: bool=True, class_: Optional[str]=None, id: Optional[str]=None, **kwargs: TagAttrValue) -> Tag:
Value box

An opinionated (:func:`~shiny.ui.card`-powered) box, designed for
displaying a `value` and `title`. Optionally, a `showcase` can provide context
for what the `value` represents (for example, it could hold an icon, or even a
:func:`~shiny.ui.output_plot`).
...
```

#### 2. Method Lookup
```bash
$ shiny docs Accordion.expect_height
# or full path:
$ shiny docs shiny.playwright.controller.Accordion.expect_height
```
```text
def expect_height(self, value: StyleValue, *, timeout: Timeout=None) -> None:
Expects the accordion to have the specified height.

Parameters
----------
value
    The expected height.
timeout
    The maximum time to wait for the height to be visible and interactable. Defaults to `None`.
```

#### 3. Multiple Lookups in One Call (Components & Controllers)
```bash
$ shiny docs shiny.ui.value_box Accordion
```
```text
def value_box(title: TagChild, value: TagChild, *args: TagChild | TagAttrs, showcase: Optional[TagChild]=None, showcase_layout: SHOWCASE_LAYOUTS_STR | ShowcaseLayout='left center', full_screen: bool=False, theme: Optional[str | ValueBoxTheme]=None, height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, max_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, min_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, fill: bool=True, class_: Optional[str]=None, id: Optional[str]=None, **kwargs: TagAttrValue) -> Tag:
Value box
...

---

class Accordion(WidthLocM, UiWithContainer):
Controller for :func:`shiny.ui.accordion`.

Methods
-------
def accordion_panel(self, data_value: str) -> AccordionPanel:
    Returns the accordion panel (:class:`~shiny.playwright.controls.AccordionPanel`)
with the specified data value.

def expect_class(self, class_name: str, *, timeout: Timeout=None) -> None:
    Expects the accordion to have the specified class.

def expect_height(self, value: StyleValue, *, timeout: Timeout=None) -> None:
    Expects the accordion to have the specified height.

def set(self, open: str | list[str], *, timeout: Timeout=None) -> None:
    Sets the state of the accordion panel.
```

#### 4. Autocomplete
```bash
$ shiny docs --complete Accordion.expect
```

title: feat(cli): Add shiny docs command for component and controller lookups
description:
## Description

Add the `shiny docs` CLI command to allow looking up documentation and signatures for Shiny components, functions, classes, and Playwright controllers in a single tool call, and integrate validation checks into runtime and startup execution (`shiny run app.py`).

### Highlights
- **Batch Lookups**: Look up multiple components in a single call, separated by `\n\n---\n\n`.
- **Controllers Support**: Full support for Playwright controllers (classes and individual methods).
- **Source Signature Extraction**: Signatures are read from AST where the component was defined, preserving full type definitions, parameter annotations, defaults, and return types on line 1.
- **Function Docstrings**: Extracts docstring from the component itself rather than file/module definitions.
- **JSON Format**: Includes `--json` flag for structured output.
- **No Categories**: AI-generated categories omitted.
- **Runtime & Startup Code Validation**: Validates Shiny apps during `shiny run app.py` for common reactivity mistakes (uncalled inputs, duplicate IDs, multiple renderers, direct input assignments, and R idioms) and raises informative runtime errors/warnings.

---

## Examples

### 1. Single Component Lookup

```bash
$ shiny docs shiny.ui.value_box
def value_box(title: TagChild, value: TagChild, *args: TagChild | TagAttrs, showcase: Optional[TagChild]=None, showcase_layout: SHOWCASE_LAYOUTS_STR | ShowcaseLayout='left center', full_screen: bool=False, theme: Optional[str | ValueBoxTheme]=None, height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, max_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, min_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, fill: bool=True, class_: Optional[str]=None, id: Optional[str]=None, **kwargs: TagAttrValue) -> Tag:
Value box

An opinionated (:func:`~shiny.ui.card`-powered) box, designed for
displaying a `value` and `title`. Optionally, a `showcase` can provide context
for what the `value` represents (for example, it could hold an icon, or even a
:func:`~shiny.ui.output_plot`).

Parameters
----------
title,value
    A string, number, or :class:`~htmltools.Tag` child to display as
    the title or value of the value box. The `title` appears above the `value`.
*args
    Unnamed arguments may be any :class:`~htmltools.Tag` children to display below
    `value`. Named arguments are passed to :func:`~shiny.ui.card` as
    element attributes.
...
```

### 2. Multiple Components Lookup in One Call

```bash
$ shiny docs shiny.ui.value_box shiny.playwright.controller.Accordion
def value_box(title: TagChild, value: TagChild, *args: TagChild | TagAttrs, showcase: Optional[TagChild]=None, showcase_layout: SHOWCASE_LAYOUTS_STR | ShowcaseLayout='left center', full_screen: bool=False, theme: Optional[str | ValueBoxTheme]=None, height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, max_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, min_height: Optional[CssUnit]=None, fill: bool=True, class_: Optional[str]=None, id: Optional[str]=None, **kwargs: TagAttrValue) -> Tag:
Value box

An opinionated (:func:`~shiny.ui.card`-powered) box, designed for
displaying a `value` and `title`. ...

---

class Accordion(WidthLocM, UiWithContainer):
Controller for :func:`shiny.ui.accordion`.

Methods
-------
def accordion_panel(self, data_value: str) -> AccordionPanel:
    Returns the accordion panel (:class:`~shiny.playwright.controls.AccordionPanel`)
with the specified data value.

def expect_class(self, class_name: str, *, timeout: Timeout=None) -> None:
    Expects the accordion to have the specified class.

def expect_height(self, value: StyleValue, *, timeout: Timeout=None) -> None:
    Expects the accordion to have the specified height.

def set(self, open: str | list[str], *, timeout: Timeout=None) -> None:
    Sets the state of the accordion panel.
```

### 3. JSON Output with `--json`

```bash
$ shiny docs --json shiny.ui.value_box shiny.playwright.controller.Accordion
[
  {
    "name": "shiny.ui.value_box",
    "signature": "def value_box(title: TagChild, value: TagChild, *args: TagChild | TagAttrs, ...) -> Tag:",
    "type": "function",
    "return_type": "Tag",
    "parameters": [
      {
        "name": "title",
        "type": "TagChild",
        "default": null,
        "kind": "POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD"
      }, ...
    ],
    "docstring": "Value box\n\n..."
  },
  ...
]
```
