title: docs: refresh conda-forge feedstock inventory in the release skill
description:
Phase 11 of the `py-shiny-release` skill said:

> Feedstocks: py-shiny and py-htmltools. py-shinyswatch and shinychat were submitted to `staged-recipes` in July 2026 (#34339, #34338) — check whether they now have feedstocks that also need bumping. py-shinywidgets and py-shinylive still do not.

That's out of date in both directions, and Phase 4 separately told the reader that shinyswatch was out of scope for Phase 11.

## What's actually true (verified 2026-08-25)

Six Shiny-ecosystem packages have conda-forge feedstocks:

| conda package | PyPI | conda-forge |
|---|---|---|
| `htmltools` | 0.7.0 | 0.7.0 |
| `shiny` | 1.7.0 | 1.7.0 |
| `shinywidgets` | 0.8.1 | 0.8.1 |
| `faicons` | 0.2.2 | 0.2.2 |
| `shiny-validate` | 0.1.3 | 0.1.3 |
| `shinychat` | 0.6.1 | 0.6.1 |
| `shinyswatch` | 0.12.0 | 0.10.0 (bump PR open) |

Four more are queued in `staged-recipes`: `shinylive` (#34628), `querychat` + `chatlas` (#34629), `brand-yml` (#34630).

## Changes

- **Phase 11** gets a feedstock inventory table keyed by the phase each package is released in, replacing the stale prose. Calls out the two naming traps: only the two oldest feedstocks carry the `py-` prefix (newer ones track the *PyPI* name, not the repo name), and `posit-dev/py-shinylive` ships to PyPI as `shinylive`, so its feedstock will be `shinylive-feedstock`.
- Documents the **dependency order** for the bumps — `htmltools` → `shiny` → downstream — since downstream recipes import `shiny` in their test phase. A downstream PR opened before `shiny` lands fails to solve; that's expected and shouldn't be "fixed."
- Adds a **pending staged-recipes** table plus a one-liner that re-checks anaconda.org, so a future session confirms current state instead of trusting the doc.
- **Phase 4**: removes the "shinyswatch has no conda-forge feedstock, so Phase 11 does not apply" note.
- **SKILL.md**: collapses the two hardcoded conda rows in the Repos table into a pointer at the Phase 11 inventory, so the list has one home rather than two that drift.

Docs-only; no code touched.

title: feat(testing): add headless simulate function and shiny simulate CLI
description:
### Overview Adds headless reactive simulation to Shiny for Python: 1. `shiny.pytest.simulate()` for fast in-memory pytest unit tests without a browser. 2. `shiny simulate` CLI command for running apps directly in the terminal. --- ### Comparison of Testing Approaches
1. Python Unit Test: shiny.pytest.simulate (~50ms per test) Runs the reactive graph directly in memory. No browser starts and no server port is opened. ```python from shiny.pytest import simulate def test_numeric_inputs(): res = simulate("app.py", inputs={"default": 20, "width": 20}) assert res.success is True assert res.outputs["default_txt"] == "20" assert res.outputs["width_txt"] == "20" ``` Best for: - Testing server logic, reactives, outputs, and calculations. - Fast local test runs and fast CI unit test suites.
2. CLI Simulation: shiny simulate (~150ms per run) Runs a simulation from the terminal or in shell scripts. Runs in an isolated subprocess with timeout protection. ```bash # Set input values and print formatted output shiny simulate app.py -i default=20 -i width=20 # Output machine-readable JSON for scripts or CI shiny simulate app.py --inputs '{"default": 20}' --json ``` Best for: - Quick sanity checks while developing in the terminal. - Shell scripts and automated CI smoke checks.
3. Playwright End-to-End Test: shiny.playwright controllers & fixtures (~2000ms per test) Uses Shiny pytest fixtures (`local_app` or `create_app_fixture`) to launch the app server and browser, paired with `shiny.playwright.controller` classes to interact with and assert on DOM components. ```python from playwright.sync_api import Page from shiny.playwright import controller from shiny.pytest import create_app_fixture from shiny.run import ShinyAppProc app = create_app_fixture("app.py") def test_numeric_inputs(page: Page, app: ShinyAppProc): page.goto(app.url) default = controller.InputNumeric(page, "default") default.expect_label("Default numeric input") default.expect_value("10") width = controller.InputNumeric(page, "width") width.set("20") width.expect_value("20") controller.OutputCode(page, "width_txt").expect_value("20") ``` Best for: - Testing browser rendering, CSS layout, and client-side JavaScript. - Verifying accessibility, keyboard focus, and browser-driven UI state.
--- ### Benchmark Comparison (5 Sample Tests) We converted 5 reactive Playwright tests to `simulate()` unit tests to compare performance: | Test Name | Playwright E2E | `shiny simulate` (CLI) | `shiny.pytest.simulate` (Unit) | Speedup vs Playwright | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `output_text` | 1.82s | 0.18s | 0.050s (49.9ms) | **36x faster** | | `output_code` | 1.91s | 0.19s | 0.052s (51.8ms) | **36x faster** | | `input_numeric_kitchensink` | 2.14s | 0.21s | 0.056s (55.7ms) | **37x faster** | | `input_action_button_kitchensink` | 2.18s | 0.22s | 0.095s (95.4ms) | **23x faster** | | `app_test_values` | 2.34s | 0.20s | 0.051s (50.5ms) | **47x faster** | | **Total Test Execution Time** | **10.39s** | **1.00s** | **0.30s (303ms)** | **34x faster (97% time reduction)** | | **Total Pytest Suite Runtime** | **10.39s** | - | **5.45s** | **1.91x faster (47.5% time reduction)** |

title: test(playwright): assert InputSelect multiple selection order
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to the discussion on #2468 / #2123.

A multiple `<select>`'s input value is always in **choices order**, never selection order — and `InputSelect.expect_selected()` asserts that same order. Nothing in the suite covered it, so the contract was only implicit.

This adds the out-of-order case to the select kitchensink: select `["Elderberry", "Apple"]` (reverse of choices order) and assert that both the controller and the server-side input value report `["Apple", "Elderberry"]`. It also adds the missing in-order `expect_selected()` assertion on the same input, which had a `.set()` but no selection assertion at all.

This mirrors the coverage `InputSelectize` already has at `tests/playwright/shiny/inputs/input_selectize/test_input_selectize.py:68-70`, where the order is *selection* order and is likewise pinned to the input value.

Not stacked on #2468: that PR's head branch lives on a fork, so a PR in this repo can't target it — and these assertions are independent of it, since it only touches `InputCheckboxGroup`.

## Testing

- `pytest -c tests/playwright/playwright-pytest.ini tests/playwright/shiny/inputs/input_kitchensink/input_select --browser chromium -q` — 2 passed
- Confirmed non-vacuous: reversing the expected list to `["Elderberry", "Apple"]` fails
- `uv run make format check-lint check-types` and `make check-pyright` — clean

title: feat: Add `ui.PageDocument` for a complete, author-owned HTML document as `App(ui=)`
description:
Closes #2462.

Adds `ui.PageDocument`, for apps whose UI is a complete HTML document the author owns — the `index.html` a JS bundler emits — rather than one Shiny builds from `ui.page_*()` components. `App` accepts one and serves it as-is: no `HTMLDocument` wrapper, which would nest `<html>` inside `<html>`.

```python
from shiny import App, ui

index_html = (Path(__file__).parent / "dist" / "index.html").read_text()
app = App(ui.PageDocument(index_html, extra_deps=[my_bundle_dep]), server)
```

It's an `HTMLTextDocument` subclass that takes **`extra_deps=`** instead of a fully specified `deps=`, and prefixes Shiny's own dependencies onto them. So app authors don't have to know or track Shiny's dependency list — which is not the three objects it looks like: `shiny_deps()` returns `shiny` (`shiny.js` + `shiny.min.css`) *and* `shiny-busy-indicators`, plus `shiny-devmode` when `SHINY_DEV_MODE=1`. Order matters too: RequireJS must load first (Shiny ships a patched copy that sets `window.define.amd = false`, so UMD-packaged libraries don't hit [mismatched anonymous define()](https://requirejs.org/docs/errors.html#mismatch)), then jQuery, which `shiny.js` is written against.

`deps_replace_pattern=` defaults to the class attribute `ui.PageDocument.DEPS_PLACEHOLDER`, so the marker is discoverable from the class rather than being a magic string app authors copy out of py-shiny's source.

**Prefixing at construction keeps every dependency in one `<script type="application/html-dependencies">` manifest.** Injecting Shiny's into an already-rendered document would emit a second manifest, and the client reads those tags with a jQuery selector plus `.text()` (`shiny/www/shared/shiny.js:7629`), which concatenates every match with no separator — two manifests glue into `shiny[1.7.0]my-dep[1.0.0]` at the seam, registering one bogus dependency and silently re-rendering the real ones. Doing it in `__init__` also means no reaching into py-htmltools private state, which an earlier revision of this PR needed.

### One place renders a UI, one place defines the dependencies

`_render_page()` is now the only place a UI is rendered, branching on what it got, and `_render_page_from_file()` folds into it. **It's also the method the UI-function path renders through**, so handling a type there is what makes it work in *both* positions — passed to `App(ui=)` directly, and returned by a UI function:

```python
App(lambda request: ui.PageDocument(index_html, extra_deps=[...]), server, bookmark_store="url")
```

That matters because bookmarking requires `App(ui=)` to be a function — `_init_bookmarking()` rejects a static UI, since the UI has to be reconstructed from the bookmarked state. So both bookmark and non-bookmark apps are covered.

The page-level dependency set now has a single definition, `html_dependencies._page_deps(include_css=)`, splatted by both page forms so they can't drift:

```python
deps=[*_page_deps(include_css=True), *(extra_deps or [])]          # ui.PageDocument
ui_res = TagList(*_page_deps(include_css=not has_bootstrap), ui)   # the tag-tree branch
```

`include_css` differs because a complete document has no tag tree to inspect for the Bootstrap dependency (whose CSS bundles Shiny's). A test renders both forms and asserts identical dependency names in identical order. `_page_deps` is deliberately not exported: its contents and ordering are exactly what we want to stay free to change, and `ui.PageDocument` covers what an app author would want it for. The other functions in `html_dependencies.py` gained docstrings.

Three things are rejected in `_render_page()`, so the errors cover the UI-function return value too, not just the direct argument:

- a plain `htmltools.HTMLTextDocument` → points at `ui.PageDocument`, instead of the `AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'get_dependencies'` from the issue;
- an `htmltools.HTMLDocument` → it hoists dependencies into `<head>` in tag-tree order and its only public mutator is `append()`, so Shiny's could only land *after* the app author's (jQuery after the scripts needing it), and appending would push it off the single-`<html>`-child path into a nested `<html>`. Pass the tags themselves instead;
- a `Path` → it names a file to read once at startup rather than a per-pageview UI value, so it stays handled in `App.__init__()`. A UI function that wants to serve a file reads it and returns a `ui.PageDocument`, making the per-request read explicit.

That invariant — every UI *value* type works in both positions, with `Path` as the deliberate exception — is written down in `.claude/references/architecture.md` under "HTML Generation and Dependencies", since it was previously unstated and easy to miss.

### R precedent

`renderPage()` has exactly this branch ([`R/shinyui.R#L31-L89`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/62d2a6c1c772415e34201c4c5a1ee85d5278bfab/R/shinyui.R#L31-L89)):

```r
  # If the ui is a NOT complete document (created by htmlTemplate()), then do some
  # preprocessing and make sure it's a complete document.
  if (!inherits(ui, "html_document")) {
    ...
  }
  shiny_deps <- c(list(jqueryDependency()), shinyDependencies())
  html <- renderDocument(ui, shiny_deps, processDep = createWebDependency)
```

When the UI already *is* a complete document, R skips the wrapping and renders it directly — and it passes its own `shiny_deps` into `renderDocument()`, which merges them with the ones the author attached via `attachDependencies()` and routes them all through `createWebDependency` (R's `_ensure_web_dependencies()`). So Shiny supplying its own dependencies, rather than the author, matches R. `shinyApp()` reaches this via `uiHttpHandler()` ([`R/shinyapp.R#L83`](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/62d2a6c1c772415e34201c4c5a1ee85d5278bfab/R/shinyapp.R#L83)).

### One thing to review

**`App(ui=Path)` now raises when the file has no dependency placeholder.** Previously the replacement silently did nothing and you got a page with no Shiny on it. Technically a behavior change for a file lacking `<meta name="shiny-dependency-placeholder" content="">`, but such an app was already broken. Easy to scope the error to the new path if you'd rather not touch `Path` behavior.

### Testing

`tests/pytest/test_app_ui_page_document.py`: Shiny's deps are added and routed; `extra_deps` share one manifest and load after `shiny.js`; a custom `deps_replace_pattern` works; a document with no placeholder raises; the document and tag-tree forms carry identical dependencies; and a plain `HTMLTextDocument`, an `HTMLDocument`, and a `Path` each raise in both positions.
